objects.definition:
#if defined(HAVE_LLU) && SIZEOF_OFF_T == 8
# define PR_LU		"llu"
# define pr_off_t	unsigned long long
#else
# define PR_LU		"lu"
# define pr_off_t	unsigned long
#endif
objects.description: Typedef-like macro defining pr_off_t as an unsigned integer type large enough for file offsets, mapped to unsigned long long when off_t is 8 bytes, otherwise unsigned long. PR_LU is the corresponding printf format suffix for that type. Used throughout ProFTPD for portable offset/size handling.
Typedef or alias not defined here. Only function declarations using unsigned long are present; no custom type is defined. This placeholder indicates there are no custom data types in this header.
Function declarations return const char*, but no custom typedef or struct is defined. Included here only to acknowledge absence of custom types.

objects.description: Forward declaration reference to the C library struct group, only a function prototype is provided when the platform lacks fgetgrent(). The struct itself is not defined here; this header merely references it. No custom type is defined by this header for group.

objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks taking three unsigned long parameters and a void * data pointer, returning int. The actual parameter list is expanded from CALLBACK_FRAME macro.

Opaque-ish primary session state structure for a ProFTPD connection, holding flags, identities, addresses, transfer bookkeeping, and pointers to control/data connections and configs. Used to track per-session information during an FTP/FTPS session.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file declares macros and function prototypes only.

IP-based binding record that associates an address/port with a default server and listening connection, plus optional name-based virtual hosts. Used by the bindings layer to manage listening sockets and routing of incoming connections. Construction and lifecycle are managed by the bindings API in this header; fields should not be modified directly by callers.
Name-based binding record mapping a hostname (possibly wildcard) to a server configuration, associated with an IP binding and port. Managed by the bindings API for virtual host name routing.
Enumeration of JSON node tags identifying the kind of value stored in a JsonNode (null, boolean, string, number, array, object). Intended to be used as the discriminator for the json_node_st union.

Node type for representing JSON values and tree structure. Each node has a tag indicating its value type and a union holding the corresponding payload (bool, string, number, or child list for arrays/objects). Parent/prev/next form intrusive links; key is set for object members. Strings must be valid UTF-8. Children for arrays/objects are maintained via the embedded children list. Lifetime is managed by API functions in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct json_node_st JsonNode;
objects.description: Typedef alias for struct json_node_st used as the primary handle to JSON nodes throughout the API.

Doubly linked-list node representing a tracked child process in ProFTPD. Holds process metadata: memory pool used by the child (pool*), OS process ID, a timestamp, a pipe file descriptor for signaling/IPC, and a flag indicating whether the child is dead. The struct participates in an intrusive list via next/prev.

Represents a Class configuration object used to group client matching rules (ACLs), satisfy policy, and arbitrary notes. Instances are linked together via cls_next. The object owns references to an allocation pool, a name, an array of pr_netacl_t rules, and a table of notes. Details on lifetime and ownership are not fully documented here; typical pattern is creation via pr_class_open(), population via setters, and finalization via pr_class_close().

Opaque command record type used by the ProFTPD command API. This header only references cmd_rec without defining its structure; it represents a parsed protocol command (e.g., FTP/HTTP/SMTP/SSH2) and is passed to functions for comparison, dispatch, and property access. Details of fields and lifecycle are unknown from this header.
Opaque memory pool type (APR-style) used for allocating cmd_rec instances and other resources. Not defined in this header.
Opaque server context/record type referenced for setting a command handler. Not defined in this header.
Opaque connection context type referenced for setting a command handler. Not defined in this header.

Configuration record node used by ProFTPD’s in-memory configuration database. Each node describes a directive/section: its type, assigned ID, arguments, flags, parent/child relationships, and owning server. Nodes are linked in a doubly-linked list and may own a subset for nested configuration contexts. Memory is allocated from pool_rec. server_struc and pool_rec are forward/externally defined elsewhere.

Controls client object holding connection/socket info, client credentials, internal flags, and a list of matched controls for a client control request. Manages one client connection to the Controls subsystem. Destruction/ownership details are not specified in this header; memory appears to be managed via the cl_pool. Unknown fields cl_next/cl_prev suggest intrusive list linkage.

Controls handler object representing a registered control action instance. Holds metadata (ID, module, action, description), scheduling (when), linkage, temp memory pool, callback and its args/responses, and client association. Flags and linkage support lifecycle and list management. Construction is via internal allocator functions; callbacks are registered with pr_ctrls_register.

objects.definition:
#ifdef HAVE_SENDFILE
typedef

# if defined(HAVE_AIX_SENDFILE) || defined(HAVE_HPUX_SENDFILE) || \
    defined(HAVE_LINUX_SENDFILE) || defined(HAVE_SOLARIS_SENDFILE)
ssize_t
# elif defined(HAVE_BSD_SENDFILE) || defined(HAVE_MACOSX_SENDFILE)
off_t
# else
#  error "You have an unknown sendfile implementation."
# endif

pr_sendfile_t;
#else
typedef ssize_t pr_sendfile_t;
#endif /* HAVE_SENDFILE */
objects.description: Typedef for the return type used by pr_data_sendfile(). It abstracts platform-specific sendfile return types: on AIX/HP-UX/Linux/Solaris it is ssize_t, on BSD/macOS it is off_t, and when HAVE_SENDFILE is not defined it defaults to ssize_t. Used to capture the differing semantics/widths of OS sendfile implementations.

TCP keepalive configuration: on/off plus idle time, probe count, and probe interval. Used to configure socket keepalive behavior via setsockopt. No constructors are declared here; instances are typically allocated and filled by server configuration code.

Represents a ProFTPD server/virtual host configuration and runtime state, including identity, network settings, TCP tuning, listener, config set, and notes. Managed as a doubly linked list via next/prev and grouped in an xaset. Memory is managed via the associated pool. Construction is performed by configuration processing elsewhere; no direct constructors are declared here.

Represents a parsed command instance being processed by the server: arguments, grouping, class, lookup cache, and per-command temporary pool. Links to the target server and applicable configuration record. Instances are ephemeral and live for the duration of handler execution using tmp_pool.

objects.definition: struct fh_rec;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration of a file-handle record type used by the display API. The actual structure is not defined in this header; it is referenced for passing handles to pr_display_fh(). Details of fields and lifecycle are unknown here.

Opaque memory pool type used by the API functions for allocation/lifetime management. It is only referenced here; no definition is provided in this header. Details such as ownership, construction, and destruction are unknown from this file.

objects.definition: typedef struct err_rec pr_error_t;
objects.description: Opaque error object handle for ProFTPD’s Error API. Actual struct err_rec is not defined in this header, making pr_error_t an incomplete/opaque type used with the provided API for creation, configuration, and formatting of error information.

Vtable of function pointers for producing human-readable explanations for specific system/library call failures. Modules register an instance to customize error messages for many operations. Implementers can supply any subset of callbacks; NULLs indicate unsupported operations.

objects.definition: typedef struct err_explain_rec pr_error_explainer_t;
objects.description: Typedef alias for struct err_explain_rec, representing an explainer vtable used by the Error API.
Opaque type referenced by the event API as the registering module handle. It is only forward-referenced here; the definition is not present in this header.

Opaque array type referenced by pr_expr_create as the return type. It is not defined in this header; likely provided by the ProFTPD memory pool/array subsystem (e.g., APR-style arrays). Since only a declaration is present here, details of layout and lifecycle are unknown.
Opaque memory pool type used for allocating objects returned by pr_expr_create. It is merely referenced here and expected to be defined in pool.h. This header does not define it.

Opaque set type referenced for filter configuration collections. It is only referenced here; no definition is provided within this header. Details about its structure and ownership semantics are unknown from this file.

Opaque memory pool type used for allocating resources and parsing flags. Only referenced in this header; no definition is provided here. Likely an APR-style or ProFTPD custom pool. Details are not available in this file.

Virtual/modular filesystem descriptor for ProFTPD. It aggregates function pointers for file and directory operations, optional extended-attribute handlers, and policy flags. Instances represent a mounted filesystem handler; they may be chained via fs_next/fs_prev. Memory is managed via fs_pool. Unknown fields like struct pool_rec are defined elsewhere.

File handle wrapper used by the FSIO layer. Encapsulates an OS file descriptor, path, owning filesystem (pr_fs_t), optional buffer and IO size hint, and a memory pool. Lifecycle is typically via pr_fsio_open/pr_fsio_close. Buffer and pool types are defined elsewhere.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only declares preprocessor macros for FTP commands and responses.

Result container for pathname globbing operations. Holds matched pathnames and optional alternative directory access callbacks when GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC is set. Fields control count, vector, reserved offsets, and flags for the run.
Large-file variant of glob_t for environments where 64-bit file status structures are used. Same semantics as glob_t but the callback signatures use dirent64/stat64 under _GNU_SOURCE.

Hook configuration struct for tpl library. Holds function pointers for logging, allocation, reallocation, free, fatal handler, and a maximum size for gather operations. Used to customize memory and error handling behavior.

Core node structure representing a mapped template element and its hierarchy for packing/unpacking. Contains type info, target address, associated data, array length, cached serialization size, and links to parent/child/sibling nodes.
Helper structure for handling binary buffers ('B' type) consisting of a pointer and its size in bytes.
State container for asynchronous or piecemeal reading of tpl images. Holds a pointer to the image buffer and its current length.

objects.description: Function type for printing/logging callbacks. Returns int; printf-like signature.

No custom types are defined in this header. The file only declares two functions (pr_help_add and pr_help_add_response) and does not introduce any structs, enums, typedefs, or classes. Types such as cmd_rec are referenced but not defined here and thus are excluded per instructions.

Primary connection structure for ProFTPD sockets. Tracks mode/state, file descriptors, network I/O streams, local/remote addressing, buffer sizing, and flags such as TCP_NODELAY usage. Memory is allocated from an APR-style pool (pool_rec).
Context object used as event payload for socket-related events, carrying the server, address, and socket descriptor.

objects.definition: typedef struct jot_filters_rec pr_jot_filters_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a set of Jot filters used to include/exclude events or variables during LogFormat resolution. The underlying struct is intentionally not exposed here.

Context passed to jotting callbacks. Carries a destination object pointer (e.g., pr_jot_parsed_t or a JSON builder) and optional user-supplied context data. Lifespan/ownership is managed by the caller; members are not owned/copied.

Scratch/state object used to accumulate the parsed representation of a LogFormat-style text. 'buf' points to the buffer, 'ptr' is the current write position, 'bufsz' is the allocated size, and 'buflen' is the current length. Caller allocates and manages memory; used by the conventional parse callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef struct json_list_st pr_json_array_t;

objects.description: Opaque JSON object handle used by the ProFTPD JSON API. The actual struct json_obj_st is not defined in this header; callers treat this as an opaque type managed via the provided API functions.

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. The only symbol provided is the function declaration `int log_lastlog(uid_t uid, const char *user_name, const char *tty, const pr_netaddr_t *remote_addr);`. Since no user-defined types are introduced here, there are no objects to document.

Opaque data record describing a single logging event/message used by ProFTPD’s logging subsystem. It carries the log type, destination file descriptor, severity/level, and the message buffer and length. Used when generating and dispatching log events to listeners.

objects.definition: typedef struct mcache_rec pr_memcache_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a memcache connection/session used by ProFTPD modules. The underlying struct mcache_rec is forward-declared only in this header, so its layout is intentionally hidden. Obtain an instance via the provided connection API and use it with the memcache item operations. Lifetime is managed by the connection functions; close when done.

objects.definition: #define PR_MKHOME_FL_USE_USER_PRIVS	0x0001
objects.description: Preprocessor macro flag indicating that user privileges (not root) should be used when creating parent directories of the home directory, useful for root-squashed NFS shares. This is a macro constant, not a data type.

Opaque handle and descriptor for a ProFTPD module. Contains module metadata, tables of handlers (configuration, command, auth), lifecycle callbacks, linkage in the global module list, and priority. Constructed/managed by the core via load/init routines; modules typically declare a static instance populated at compile time.
Return record from a module handler. Conveys whether the handler declined, handled successfully, or returned an error, with optional numeric code, message, and opaque data pointer.
Configuration directive table entry associating a directive string with a handler and back-reference to the owning module. Arrays of these define a module's config directives.

Command table entry defining a command name, type, grouping, handler callback, auth requirements, legacy transfer-interrupt flag, class bitmask, and owning module pointer. Modules provide arrays of these for supported commands.
Authentication handler table entry for naming and registering an auth check handler with optional flags and a back-reference to the owning module.

objects.definition: typedef struct pr_netacl_t pr_netacl_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a network ACL (access-control list) used by ProFTPD to represent address/name-based allow/deny rules. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the concrete struct layout is private to the implementation.
Enumeration of network ACL matching types: match all, none, IP mask (CIDR/netmask), exact IP match, DNS name match, IP glob, and DNS glob. Used to describe how a pr_netacl_t evaluates inputs.

Opaque network address holder used by ProFTPD. Encapsulates address family, cached DNS and IP string forms, and a sockaddr union for IPv4 (and optionally IPv6). Used throughout the Netaddr API for allocation, comparison, conversion, and querying. Memory is typically managed via ProFTPD pools; callers should not free directly.

objects.definition: typedef struct netaddr_struc pr_netaddr_t;
objects.description: Typedef alias for struct netaddr_struc used as the public handle for network addresses within ProFTPD.

Local fallback definition of struct addrinfo (compatible with POSIX getaddrinfo) used when the system does not provide it. Holds hints/results for address resolution, including flags, family, socket type, protocol, address length, canonical name, socket address, and linkage to the next result.
Fixed-layout buffer object used by the NetIO layer to track a memory buffer, its total size, current position, and remaining bytes.
NetIO provider object that encapsulates function pointers (callbacks) implementing the I/O behavior for streams, plus metadata about the registering module.
Represents a single network I/O stream (control, data, or other). Tracks FD, mode, polling interval/flags, associated buffer, per-stream notes, and the NetIO provider used.

Blowfish cipher context holding the 4 S-boxes and the P-array (subkeys). Used with the provided Blowfish init/expand/enc/dec APIs to perform encryption and decryption. The S and P arrays must be initialized before use via Blowfish_initstate and key expansion routines (e.g., blf_key).

Holds the results of parsing a single line of ProFTPD configuration: the constructed cmd_rec to dispatch to config handlers, the original text line, and its source file and line number. Useful for tracking origin and content of parsed directives. The lifetime/ownership of the cmd_rec is external (allocated from a pool passed to the parser).

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only declares functions for pidfile handling: pr_pidfile_get, pr_pidfile_set, pr_pidfile_remove, pr_pidfile_write. This placeholder object notes the absence of user-defined types.

objects.description: Opaque memory pool handle used by ProFTPD's pooled allocator. Actual struct layout is intentionally hidden; only a forward typedef is provided here.
Structure describing debugging/statistics information for a pool, optionally including per-pool, freelist, and total counters. Used with pr_pool_debug_memory2().
Resizable array container whose storage is allocated from a pool. Tracks element size, current count, capacity, and data pointer.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only declares functions related to process title handling.
No custom data types are defined in this header. It only declares two functions: pr_random_init and pr_random_next. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to document.

objects.definition: typedef struct redis_rec pr_redis_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a Redis connection used by ProFTPD modules. The underlying struct redis_rec is not defined in this header, making pr_redis_t an incomplete, opaque type intended to be managed via the provided API functions.

objects.definition: typedef struct regexp_rec pr_regex_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a compiled regular expression used by ProFTPD. It is a typedef to an incomplete struct (struct regexp_rec), making it an opaque type whose internals are hidden from callers. Instances are allocated via pr_regexp_alloc() and freed via pr_regexp_free(). The underlying implementation abstracts over POSIX and PCRE/PCRE2 engines.
Linked-list node representing a queued FTP response. Each node holds the numeric reply code (num), the reply text (msg), and a next pointer for chaining responses to be flushed to the client.

Opaque header record written at the start of a ProFTPD scoreboard file. Contains a magic value, a version for compatibility checks, the owning daemon PID (or 0 for inetd), and the time the header was written. Used to validate and introspect scoreboard files.

A single process/session entry written to the scoreboard. Captures process/user IDs, server and client addressing, user/class/protocol, current working directory, current command and argument, session/idle timestamps, and transfer metrics (planned size, completed bytes, total bytes, and elapsed time). Used by utilities and server code to monitor session state and progress.

Doubly linked list node used as the membership element within an XAset container. Each member embeds next/prev pointers for linkage. Details of payload are not defined here; typical usage is to embed this as the first field in a larger struct to participate in the set/list.
Container representing a set (internally a linked list) of xasetmember_t nodes. It maintains a head pointer, an associated memory pool, and an optional comparison function for ordered insertions.

objects.definition: typedef int (*XASET_COMPARE)(xasetmember_t *v1, xasetmember_t *v2);

objects.definition: typedef xasetmember_t* (*XASET_MCOPY)(xasetmember_t *mem);

Enumeration typedef classifying stash symbol categories used by ProFTPD's symbol table ("stash"). Values indicate the type of symbol being added/queried/removed: configuration directives (PR_SYM_CONF), commands (PR_SYM_CMD), authentication APIs (PR_SYM_AUTH), and hooks (PR_SYM_HOOK). Used as an argument to the pr_stash_* APIs to select the symbol domain.
Opaque memory pool type used throughout ProFTPD/APR-like APIs. It is referenced here as a parameter type; its definition is not present in this header.
Opaque dynamic array descriptor type used by ProFTPD/APR-like APIs. It is referenced here; its definition is not present in this header.

GNU-style long option descriptor used by getopt_long(). Only defined here when HAVE_GETOPT and HAVE_GETOPT_LONG are not available. Describes a long option name, whether it takes an argument, an optional flag location to set, and the value to return.

Internal node representing a hashed table key. Holds the key bytes, size, cached hash, entry count for that key, and a link to the next key in a chain. Used by the table implementation; not intended for external manipulation.

Internal table entry linking a key to a stored value. Supports doubly-linked chaining, an index within its chain, pointer to the associated key node, and value bytes/size. Used internally by table operations.

objects.definition: typedef struct table_rec pr_table_t;
objects.description: Opaque hash table type managed by the ProFTPD core. Stores key/value entries and supports optional multi-value per key and caching behaviors. The concrete struct is intentionally hidden; interact via the pr_table_* APIs.
Opaque type referenced as the owner of a scheduled timer. It is not defined in this header; it is declared/defined elsewhere in the codebase. Details unknown here.
Function callback type used by the timer subsystem for timer expiry callbacks. The actual typedef is not defined in this header; it is declared/defined elsewhere. Details unknown here.

Opaque table type referenced by the Trace API, presumably a ProFTPD core data structure representing a key/value table or hash. It is only forward-declared (referenced) here; no definition is present in this header. Details about construction, fields, and lifetime are unknown in this file.

No custom types are defined in this header. It only declares functions for UTF-8 encode/decode and internal init/free routines. All parameter/return types (char, size_t, int) are built-in or referenced from elsewhere (e.g., pool) and not defined here.

Opaque memory pool type used throughout ProFTPD for memory management. It is referenced here as a parameter to pr_var_set(), but is not defined in this header. Details of construction and lifetime are managed elsewhere in the codebase.

functions.name: pr_version_get_module_api_number
functions.description: Returns the ProFTPD module API version number currently compiled into the server. Use this to compare a module’s expected API level against the server’s API to ensure compatibility (e.g., for load-time checks). Details on the exact numeric encoding are not documented here; typically this corresponds to PR_MODULE_API_VERSION.
requirements: No arguments required.
May be called at any time after program start; no initialization requirements are documented.
Return value is an unsigned long integer representing the module API version; callers should not assume more semantics than version comparison unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: pr_version_get_number
functions.description: Returns the ProFTPD server version number as a machine-usable integer constant corresponding to the compiled version (e.g., derived from PROFTPD_VERSION_NUMBER). Use for numeric version checks and comparisons.
requirements: No arguments required.
May be called at any time after program start; no initialization requirements are documented.
Return value is an unsigned long integer; callers should treat it as an opaque version code unless they know the encoding scheme.

functions.name: pr_version_get_str
functions.description: Returns the ProFTPD server version as a human-readable, null-terminated string corresponding to the compiled version (e.g., similar to PROFTPD_VERSION_TEXT). Useful for logs, diagnostics, and display.
requirements: No arguments required.
Returned pointer refers to immutable storage; do not modify the string.
Caller must not free the returned pointer; lifetime and ownership remain with the library.
May be called at any time after program start; no initialization requirements are documented.
Caller should treat the content as read-only and persistent for at least the duration of the process unless documented otherwise.

functions.name: pr_fnmatch
functions.signature: int pr_fnmatch(const char *pattern, const char *string, int flags);
functions.description: Filename glob-style pattern match. Compares string against pattern using optional flags similar to fnmatch(3). Supports flags such as PR_FNM_PATHNAME, PR_FNM_NOESCAPE, PR_FNM_PERIOD, PR_FNM_LEADING_DIR, PR_FNM_CASEFOLD, and PR_FNM_EXTMATCH. Returns 0 on match and PR_FNM_NOMATCH on no match; other nonzero values may indicate errors (details not documented here). Use to test whether a path or name matches a shell-style pattern.
requirements: pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.
string must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string.
flags is a bitwise OR of PR_FNM_* constants; pass 0 for default behavior.
If PR_FNM_PATHNAME is set, wildcards will not match '/'.
If PR_FNM_NOESCAPE is set, backslash escaping of special chars is disabled.
If PR_FNM_PERIOD is set, a leading '.' in string only matches explicitly.
If PR_FNM_LEADING_DIR is set, a match is valid even if string has trailing '/...'.
If PR_FNM_CASEFOLD is set, comparison is case-insensitive.
If PR_FNM_EXTMATCH is set, ksh-like extended patterns are enabled.

functions.name: sstrncpy
functions.signature: int sstrncpy(char *dst, const char *src, size_t dstsize);
functions.description: Safe string copy helper (ProFTPD-specific). Copies src into dst, bounded by dstsize, ensuring destination buffer limits are respected. Exact return convention is not documented here; based on name/signature it likely indicates success or truncation. Use as a safer alternative to strcpy/strncpy when copying into fixed-size buffers.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable buffer of at least dstsize bytes.
src must be a valid, NUL-terminated string.
dstsize should reflect the total capacity of dst; passing 0 results in no copying.
Behavior on truncation and the exact return value are unknown from this header; callers should check the return value and handle possible truncation.

functions.name: pr_gai_strerror
functions.description: Wrapper for gai_strerror(3). Returns a human-readable string describing a getaddrinfo(3)/getnameinfo(3) EAI_* error code. If the system provides gai_strerror, this name may be defined as a macro alias to the system function.
requirements: eai_error should be a valid EAI_* error code returned by getaddrinfo/getnameinfo.
Return value points to a static string; it must not be modified or freed.
Thread-safety and locale of the returned string follow the underlying gai_strerror implementation.

functions.name: fgetpwent
functions.description: POSIX function to read the next passwd entry from an open stream. Parses one struct passwd from the current position in the file (e.g., a file in passwd(5) format) and advances the stream. Returns a pointer to a static struct passwd or NULL on EOF/error.
requirements: stream must be a valid FILE* opened for reading on a passwd-format file.
The returned struct passwd may point to static storage that can be overwritten by subsequent calls; copy fields if you need to keep them.
On error or end-of-file, returns NULL; callers should check errno/feof as appropriate.

functions.name: fgetgrent
functions.description: POSIX function to read the next group entry from an open stream. Parses one struct group from the current position in the file (e.g., a file in group(5) format) and advances the stream. Returns a pointer to a static struct group or NULL on EOF/error.
requirements: stream must be a valid FILE* opened for reading on a group-format file.
The returned struct group may point to static storage that can be overwritten by subsequent calls; copy fields if you need to keep them.
On error or end-of-file, returns NULL; callers should check errno/feof as appropriate.

functions.name: hstrerror
functions.description: Legacy resolver function that converts a h_errno code to a human-readable string. Use to format errors from gethostbyname/gethostbyaddr and similar legacy resolver calls. Some systems provide this function natively; otherwise ProFTPD provides a replacement.
requirements: herrno_code should be a valid h_errno value (e.g., HOST_NOT_FOUND, TRY_AGAIN, NO_RECOVERY, NO_DATA).
Return value points to a static string; it must not be modified or freed.

functions.name: mkstemp
functions.description: Creates and opens a unique temporary file, replacing the trailing XXXXXX in template with a unique suffix, and returns an open file descriptor with mode 0600. This is a drop-in replacement if the system lacks mkstemp(3).
requirements: template must be a writable, NUL-terminated string ending with at least six consecutive 'X' characters.
The buffer backing template must be large enough to be modified in place; on success, those Xs are replaced by the unique name.
Returns an open file descriptor >= 0 on success and -1 on error; callers must close the descriptor when done.
The directory containing template must exist and be writable by the process.

functions.name: snprintf
functions.signature: int snprintf(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: C99-formatted printing into a fixed-size buffer. Writes formatted output to str, writing at most size bytes (including the terminating NUL). Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the NUL), allowing detection of truncation.
requirements: str must be a valid writable buffer of at least size bytes (unless size is 0).
format must be a valid printf-style format string with corresponding arguments.
If size is 0, no bytes are written and str may be NULL by convention, but portability varies; safest is to pass a non-NULL str when size > 0.
Callers must check the return value to detect truncation (return >= size indicates truncation).

functions.name: strsep
functions.description: Tokenizes a string in place, splitting at any delimiter characters. On each call, returns the next token and updates *stringp to point past the delimiter or to NULL at end. Unlike strtok, it can return empty tokens and is reentrant if used on separate strings.
requirements: stringp must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* that points to a mutable, NUL-terminated string (or is NULL to indicate no more tokens).
delim must be a valid, NUL-terminated string of delimiter characters; must not be NULL.
The string referenced by *stringp will be modified (delimiters replaced by NUL).
Returns NULL when no tokens remain (i.e., when *stringp is NULL on entry).

functions.name: vsnprintf
functions.signature: int vsnprintf(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list-based variant of snprintf. Writes formatted output to str using the variable argument list ap, writing at most size bytes (including the terminating NUL). Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the NUL).
requirements: str must be a valid writable buffer of at least size bytes (unless size is 0).
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
ap must be a valid, initialized va_list for the provided format.
Callers must check the return value to detect truncation (return >= size indicates truncation).
ap usage must follow va_start/va_end rules in the caller; it may be reused only as permitted by the platform.

functions.name: session_exit
functions.description: Ends/tears down the current FTP session and performs any necessary cleanup. The two int parameters and two void* parameters are opaque here; their exact semantics are not documented in this header. Based on the name and typical ProFTPD lifecycle, this is intended to be invoked when a session is terminating (e.g., normal logout, error, or signal-triggered shutdown).
requirements: Intended to be called at the end of a session life cycle (inferred from the name).
Argument meanings and valid ranges are unknown in this header; treat the void* parameters as opaque context pointers.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; typical usage would be from the session/connection-handling context.

functions.name: set_daemon_rlimits
functions.description: Configures process resource limits (rlimits) for the ProFTPD daemon process. Typically used during daemon startup to set limits such as max open files, memory, or core size before spawning/servicing sessions.
requirements: Should be called in the daemon (master) context rather than a per-session child (inferred from the name).
May require sufficient privileges to raise certain resource limits; behavior on failure is not specified here.
Must be called on a platform that supports rlimits; exact limits adjusted are not documented in this header.

functions.name: set_session_rlimits
functions.description: Configures process resource limits (rlimits) appropriate for an individual FTP session. Typically called after a session process is created to constrain or adjust resources for that session.
requirements: Should be called in the per-session process context, not the daemon/master (inferred from the name).
May require sufficient privileges to change certain limits; behavior on failure is not specified here.
Platform- and configuration-dependent; exact limits changed are not documented in this header.

functions.name: pr_ascii_ftp_reset
functions.description: Reset internal state used for FTP ASCII conversion rules. Intended to clear any conversion carry-over or state between separate conversions or transfers. Exact state semantics are not documented here.
requirements: unknown: No explicit caller requirements are documented in this header.

functions.name: pr_ascii_ftp_from_crlf
functions.signature: int pr_ascii_ftp_from_crlf(pool *p, char *in, size_t inlen, char **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Convert an input buffer from FTP-style CRLF line endings to LF-only. Processes the input byte-by-byte, writing converted data into a newly produced output buffer and returning the number of trailing "carry over" CR characters that could not be paired with an LF (e.g., a CR at the end of the input). On success, sets *out to the converted buffer, *outlen to the number of bytes written, and returns the carry-over count; on error, returns -1 and sets errno.
requirements: in must point to at least inlen bytes (inferred from signature).
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* to receive the allocated output buffer (inferred from signature).
outlen must be a non-NULL pointer to a size_t to receive the output length (inferred from signature).
p must be a valid/initialized memory pool object (allocation strategy is not documented; typical ProFTPD convention suggests pool-based allocation) (inferred from library patterns).
Caller must check the return value: -1 indicates error and errno is set; non-negative indicates success and represents the number of carry-over CRs.

functions.name: pr_ascii_ftp_to_crlf
functions.signature: int pr_ascii_ftp_to_crlf(pool *p, char *in, size_t inlen, char **out, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Convert an input buffer to FTP-style CRLF line endings. Produces a newly allocated output buffer, sets *outlen to the number of bytes written, and returns a non-negative integer N on success (exact meaning of N is not specified here). On error, returns -1 and sets errno. Note: This function deliberately uses malloc(3) for the output buffer (see Bug#4352).
requirements: in must point to at least inlen bytes (inferred from signature).
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a char* to receive the allocated output buffer.
outlen must be a non-NULL pointer to a size_t to receive the output length.
Caller MUST free(*out) using free(3) when done (explicitly documented).
Caller must check the return value: -1 indicates error and errno is set; non-negative indicates success (exact meaning of the value N is unspecified by this header).
p is accepted but the output allocation is performed via malloc(3) (explicitly documented).

functions.name: pr_auth_setpwent
functions.description: Initializes or rewinds the ProFTPD auth user-entry enumeration (passwd-like) for subsequent pr_auth_getpwent() calls, using the provided memory pool for any allocations.
requirements: The pool pointer must reference a valid, live ProFTPD pool.
Call before the first pr_auth_getpwent() to start enumeration, or to rewind after reaching the end.
Do not destroy the pool while iterating entries.

functions.name: pr_auth_endpwent
functions.description: Terminates/cleans up any state associated with user-entry (passwd) enumeration started via pr_auth_setpwent()/pr_auth_getpwent().
requirements: The pool must be the same pool used for pr_auth_setpwent()/pr_auth_getpwent() operations, and must be valid at the time of call.
After this call, further pr_auth_getpwent() calls require pr_auth_setpwent() again.

functions.name: pr_auth_setgrent
functions.description: Initializes or rewinds the ProFTPD auth group-entry enumeration (group-like) for subsequent pr_auth_getgrent() calls, using the provided pool for allocations.
requirements: The pool pointer must reference a valid, live ProFTPD pool.
Call before the first pr_auth_getgrent() to start enumeration, or to rewind after reaching the end.
Do not destroy the pool while iterating entries.

functions.name: pr_auth_endgrent
functions.description: Terminates/cleans up any state associated with group-entry enumeration started via pr_auth_setgrent()/pr_auth_getgrent().
requirements: The pool must be the same pool used for pr_auth_setgrent()/pr_auth_getgrent() operations, and must be valid at the time of call.
After this call, further pr_auth_getgrent() calls require pr_auth_setgrent() again.

functions.name: pr_auth_getpwent
functions.description: Retrieves the next user (passwd) entry in the enumeration sequence, allocating any returned data from the given pool.
requirements: Call pr_auth_setpwent(pool*) before the first call to start enumeration.
The pool must be valid and remain alive while using the returned struct passwd.
Stop when the function indicates no more entries (return value or contents not specified in this header; exact end-of-list behavior is unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_getgrent
functions.description: Retrieves the next group entry in the enumeration sequence, allocating any returned data from the given pool.
requirements: Call pr_auth_setgrent(pool*) before the first call to start enumeration.
The pool must be valid and remain alive while using the returned struct group.
Stop when the function indicates no more entries (exact end-of-list behavior is unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_getpwnam
functions.description: Looks up a user (passwd) entry by login name, returning a struct passwd allocated out of the provided pool.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live for the lifetime of the returned data.
The user name pointer must be non-NULL and point to a NUL-terminated string.
Behavior on not found (NULL vs error) is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_getpwuid
functions.description: Looks up a user (passwd) entry by UID, returning a struct passwd allocated from the given pool.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live for the lifetime of the returned data.
Behavior on not found (NULL vs error) is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_getgrnam
functions.description: Looks up a group entry by group name, returning a struct group allocated from the given pool.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live for the lifetime of the returned data.
The group name pointer must be non-NULL and point to a NUL-terminated string.
Behavior on not found (NULL vs error) is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_getgrgid
functions.description: Looks up a group entry by GID, returning a struct group allocated from the given pool.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live for the lifetime of the returned data.
Behavior on not found (NULL vs error) is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_authenticate
functions.signature: int pr_auth_authenticate(pool *, const char *, const char *);
functions.description: Authenticates a user using the provided username and password against the configured ProFTPD authentication backends. Returns one of the PR_AUTH_* status codes defined in this header (e.g., PR_AUTH_OK, PR_AUTH_BADPWD, PR_AUTH_NOPWD, etc.).
requirements: The pool must be valid for any internal allocations.
Username and password pointers must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated strings.
Callers must handle all documented PR_AUTH_* return codes (including error/insufficient credential cases).

functions.name: pr_auth_authorize
functions.description: Performs authorization checks for the given username after authentication, according to server configuration (e.g., access rules). Returns a PR_AUTH_* status code.
requirements: The pool must be valid for any internal allocations.
Username must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Callers must handle PR_AUTH_* return codes; exact mapping of codes to authorization outcomes beyond comments is partially unknown.

functions.name: pr_auth_check
functions.signature: int pr_auth_check(pool *, const char *, const char *, const char *);
functions.description: Performs a combined authentication/authorization check for a user. Parameters are likely username, password, and an additional context (e.g., service/class), but exact semantics are not documented here (unknown). Returns a PR_AUTH_* status code.
requirements: The pool must be valid for any internal allocations.
All const char* parameters supplied must be valid NUL-terminated strings (exact meanings are unknown).
Callers must handle PR_AUTH_* return codes.

functions.name: pr_auth_uid2name
functions.description: Resolves a UID to a username string, allocating the result from the given pool. May use internal caching depending on configuration.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live while using the returned string.
Caller must handle the case where no name exists for the UID (return behavior not specified; unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_gid2name
functions.description: Resolves a GID to a group name string, allocating the result from the given pool. May use internal caching depending on configuration.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live while using the returned string.
Caller must handle the case where no name exists for the GID (return behavior not specified; unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_name2uid
functions.description: Resolves a username to a UID using configured auth backends and caches. The pool is used for transient allocations if needed.
requirements: The pool must be valid.
Username must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle the case where the name does not map to a UID (exact error/sentinel value not specified; unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_name2gid
functions.description: Resolves a group name to a GID using configured auth backends and caches. The pool is used for transient allocations if needed.
requirements: The pool must be valid.
Group name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle the case where the name does not map to a GID (exact error/sentinel value not specified; unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_getgroups
functions.signature: int pr_auth_getgroups(pool *, const char *, array_header **, array_header **);
functions.description: Retrieves group membership information for a user. Populates one or more array_header outputs with group data (exact array contents/semantics not detailed here). Returns status as int (exact values unknown).
requirements: The pool must be valid for allocations.
The username must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Output pointer parameters (array_header**) should be non-NULL if results are desired; the function may write allocated arrays to them.
Caller must be prepared for an error indication via the return value (exact conventions unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_requires_pass
functions.description: Determines whether the given user requires a password during login, based on configuration (e.g., anonymous or RFC2228 contexts). Returns an int flag (exact values not described; likely nonzero/zero).
requirements: The pool must be valid.
Username must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must interpret the returned int per module conventions (exact semantics are partially unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_get_anon_config
functions.description: Convenience function to retrieve the <Anonymous> configuration applicable to a given login name. If the user should not be treated as anonymous, returns NULL. May update login_user, real_user, and anon_user to reflect mapping/handling.
requirements: The pool p must be valid for allocations.
login_user must be a non-NULL pointer to a const char*; the function may update the pointed-to value.
real_user and anon_user must be non-NULL char** if the caller expects them to be set; the function may write to these pointers.
Caller must handle a NULL return indicating non-anonymous handling.

functions.name: pr_auth_chroot
functions.description: Wrapper around chroot(2) that also manages any necessary environment setup for ProFTPD. Returns the result of the operation as an int (standard chroot semantics: 0 on success, -1 on error with errno).
requirements: The path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string designating the new root directory.
The process must have sufficient privileges to perform chroot (usually root).
The target directory should exist and be accessible; standard chroot constraints apply.

functions.name: pr_auth_banned_by_ftpusers
functions.description: Checks the /etc/ftpusers file, per the UseFtpUsers directive, to determine if the given user is banned. Returns TRUE if banned, FALSE if not banned, and -1 on error.
requirements: The xaset_t* (server/config context) must be valid and appropriately initialized for reading the directive state.
Username must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle three-way return: TRUE (banned), FALSE (not banned), and -1 (error).

functions.name: pr_auth_is_valid_shell
functions.description: Validates the user's shell against /etc/shells per the RequireValidShell directive. Returns TRUE if valid, FALSE if invalid, and -1 on error.
requirements: The xaset_t* (server/config context) must be valid and appropriately initialized for reading the directive state.
Shell path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle three-way return: TRUE (valid), FALSE (invalid), and -1 (error).

functions.name: pr_auth_add_auth_only_module
functions.description: Adds a module name to the list of authenticating-only modules (e.g., PAM) used during authentication. Returns status as int (exact conventions not specified).
requirements: Module name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Callers should ensure the module name corresponds to a loaded/known module; exact validation rules are unknown.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (exact values unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_remove_auth_only_module
functions.description: Removes the named module from the authenticating-only modules list. Returns status as int (exact conventions not specified).
requirements: Module name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (exact values unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_clear_auth_only_modules
functions.description: Clears the list of authenticating-only modules, typically after authentication completes. Returns status as int (exact conventions not specified).
requirements: Call at an appropriate point in the auth lifecycle (e.g., after authentication).
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (exact values unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_cache_clear
functions.description: Clears any cached IDs/names in the Auth API cache.
requirements: Safe to call when no other threads/tasks depend on cached lookups; concurrency semantics are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_cache_set
functions.signature: int pr_auth_cache_set(int enable, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Enables or disables caching of certain data within the Auth API, controlled by the bitmask flags PR_AUTH_CACHE_FL_*. Returns status as int.
requirements: The enable argument acts as a boolean toggle (nonzero enable, zero disable).
flags is a bitwise OR of PR_AUTH_CACHE_FL_* values; PR_AUTH_CACHE_FL_DEFAULT provides a recommended set.
Callers must check the return value for success/failure (exact values unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_get_home
functions.description: Retrieves the user's home directory, applying any RewriteHome configuration. Returns a directory path string allocated from the given pool.
requirements: The pool must be valid and live while using the returned string.
pw_dir must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string (the base home directory).
Caller must handle cases where rewriting yields the same or a different path; behavior on failure (NULL?) is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: pr_auth_set_max_password_len
functions.description: Sets the policy for the maximum allowable password length (to mitigate crypt(3) resource consumption). Returns the effective configured maximum length.
requirements: The pool p must be valid.
len specifies the desired maximum length; acceptable range and special values are not specified in this header (unknown).
Callers must use the returned size_t as the active limit.

functions.name: pr_auth_bcrypt
functions.signature: char *pr_auth_bcrypt(pool *p, const char *key, const char *salt, size_t *hashed_len);
functions.description: Pool-using convenience wrapper for bcrypt(). Generates a hashed string for the given key and salt. The result is allocated from the provided pool; hashed_len, if non-NULL, is set to the length of the resulting hash.
requirements: The pool p must be valid and live for the lifetime of the returned string.
key and salt must be non-NULL NUL-terminated strings suitable for bcrypt (exact format/length constraints depend on bcrypt and are not specified here).
hashed_len may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to writable storage.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect errors (exact error conditions not specified).

functions.name: pr_ipbind_accept_conn
functions.description: Accepts an incoming connection on one of the listening fds in readfds and returns the conn_t for the binding associated with the ready fd. Returns NULL if not found or on invalid arguments. Typical use is after select() indicates readability on listening sockets.
requirements: readfds must not be NULL
listenfd must not be NULL and will be set to the accepted listening fd on success
The file descriptors set in readfds must be valid listening sockets previously opened by the bindings layer
Caller must check for NULL return to handle errors/not found

functions.name: pr_ipbind_create
functions.signature: int pr_ipbind_create(server_rec *server, const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Creates a new IP-based binding for server at addr:port and adds it to the bindings list. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: server must not be NULL
addr must not be NULL
port must be a valid TCP/UDP port number (1–65535)
Caller must check for a -1 return to detect failure before proceeding to open/listen

functions.name: pr_ipbind_close
functions.signature: int pr_ipbind_close(const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port, unsigned char close_namebinds);
functions.description: Closes all IP bindings for the given addr:port and marks them inactive so future lookups can skip them. Optionally closes associated namebinds. Returns 0 on success, -1 if no associated bindings were found or on error.
requirements: addr must not be NULL
port must match the target binding(s) to close
If close_namebinds is nonzero, associated name-based bindings will be closed as well
Caller must handle -1 return (e.g., when no bindings exist)

functions.name: pr_ipbind_close_listeners
functions.description: Closes all listening fds maintained by the bindings layer. Intended to be called just after a process has been forked to handle a session. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: Should be called in the child process immediately after fork to avoid inheriting listening sockets
Caller must handle the return value and any resulting inability to accept new connections in the child

functions.name: pr_ipbind_add_binds
functions.description: Scans server’s configuration for bind directives and creates additional IP bindings accordingly. Honors SocketBindTight if configured. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (e.g., server == NULL).
requirements: server must not be NULL
Caller must check for -1 return and avoid assuming binds were added on failure

functions.name: pr_ipbind_find
functions.signature: pr_ipbind_t *pr_ipbind_find(const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port, unsigned char skip_inactive);
functions.description: Searches the binding list and returns the pr_ipbind_t matching addr:port. If skip_inactive is nonzero, inactive bindings are ignored. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: addr must not be NULL
port identifies the target binding
Caller must handle NULL return when no matching binding exists
If skip_inactive is nonzero, inactive bindings will not be returned

functions.name: pr_ipbind_get
functions.description: Iterator over the binding list. Given a previous binding, returns the next; if prev is NULL, iteration restarts at the beginning. Returns NULL when the end is reached.
requirements: prev may be NULL to start/restart iteration; otherwise it must be a pointer previously returned by this iterator
Returned pr_ipbind_t pointers are owned by the bindings layer and must not be modified or freed by the caller

functions.name: pr_ipbind_get_server
functions.description: Returns the server_rec bound to the specified addr:port. Returns NULL if no match is found.
requirements: addr must not be NULL
Caller must handle NULL return if there is no server for the given addr:port

functions.name: pr_ipbind_listen
functions.description: Waits on the given fd_set of listening sockets and returns the fd that has an incoming connection ready. Returns -1 on error (e.g., readfds is NULL).
requirements: readfds must not be NULL
The fds in readfds must be valid listening sockets prepared by pr_ipbind_open
Caller must handle -1 return and not assume a valid fd on error

functions.name: pr_ipbind_open
functions.signature: int pr_ipbind_open(const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port, conn_t *listen_conn, unsigned char isdefault, unsigned char islocalhost, unsigned char open_namebinds);
functions.description: Prepares the IP-based binding at addr:port for listening, optionally marking it as the default and/or localhost binding, and optionally opening associated namebinds. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: addr must not be NULL
port must be a valid port for which a binding exists or is being opened
listen_conn must be a valid conn_t to associate as the listener (library-specific; must be initialized)
isdefault indicates whether this binding is the DefaultServer binding
islocalhost indicates whether this binding handles localhost requests
If open_namebinds is nonzero, associated namebinds will be opened
Caller must check for -1 return and avoid using an uninitialized listener on failure

functions.name: pr_ipbind_get_listening_conn
functions.signature: conn_t *pr_ipbind_get_listening_conn(server_rec *server, const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Retrieves the listening conn_t associated with server at addr:port. Returns NULL if none is found.
requirements: server must not be NULL
addr must not be NULL
Caller must handle NULL return when no listening connection exists for the inputs

functions.name: pr_namebind_close
functions.description: Closes the name-based binding (pr_namebind_t) identified by name and associated with addr. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: name must not be NULL or empty
addr must not be NULL
Caller must check for -1 return when the named binding does not exist or cannot be closed

functions.name: pr_namebind_create
functions.signature: int pr_namebind_create(server_rec *server, const char *name, pr_ipbind_t *ipbind, const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Creates a name-based binding mapping name (usually a DNS hostname) to server, associated with ipbind and addr:port. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: server must not be NULL
name must not be NULL or empty and should be a valid hostname
ipbind must not be NULL and should correspond to the given addr
addr must not be NULL
port must be a valid port number (1–65535)
Caller must check for -1 return before attempting to open or use the namebind

functions.name: pr_namebind_find
functions.signature: pr_namebind_t *pr_namebind_find(const char *name, const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port, unsigned char skip_inactive);
functions.description: Searches the bindings layer for a pr_namebind_t matching name at addr:port. If skip_inactive is nonzero, inactive namebinds are ignored. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: name must not be NULL or empty
addr must not be NULL
Caller must handle NULL return when no matching namebind exists
If skip_inactive is nonzero, inactive namebinds will not be returned

functions.name: pr_namebind_get_server
functions.signature: server_rec *pr_namebind_get_server(const char *name, const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Finds and returns the server_rec associated with the given name at addr:port. If none is found, the server_rec of the containing pr_ipbind_t is used. Returns NULL if neither exists.
requirements: name must not be NULL or empty
addr must not be NULL
Caller must be prepared for the fallback behavior (defaulting to the server of the IP binding) and handle a possible NULL if no binding exists

functions.name: pr_namebind_open
functions.signature: int pr_namebind_open(const char *name, const pr_netaddr_t *addr, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Opens (activates) the name-based binding identified by name for the given addr:port. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: name must not be NULL or empty
addr must not be NULL
port must be valid (1–65535)
Caller must check for -1 return and not assume the namebind is active on failure

functions.name: pr_namebind_count
functions.description: Returns the number of namebinds associated with the given server_rec.
requirements: The server_rec pointer must not be NULL
Caller must not rely on the count remaining stable if bindings are concurrently modified

functions.name: init_bindings
functions.description: Initializes the Bindings layer. Must be called before using any of the bindings APIs.
requirements: Must be called once before creating, opening, or searching bindings
Not thread-safe initialization unless documented elsewhere; avoid concurrent initialization
Do not call other bindings functions before initialization

functions.name: free_bindings
functions.description: Frees resources held by the Bindings layer.
requirements: Should be called during shutdown/cleanup after bindings are no longer needed
After calling, previously returned pr_ipbind_t/pr_namebind_t/conn_t pointers from this layer must not be used
Do not call other bindings APIs after freeing, unless init_bindings is called again

functions.name: json_decode
functions.description: Parses a JSON-encoded C string into a heap-allocated JsonNode tree. Use this to turn raw JSON text into the in-memory representation used by this API. Free the resulting tree with json_delete when done. Details of error reporting and return-on-error behavior are not documented here; typical behavior is to return NULL on parse failure.
requirements: json must be a NUL-terminated C string.
json should contain valid JSON text; deeply nested inputs may be limited by CCAN_JSON_MAX_DEPTH (default 16).
Caller is responsible for eventually freeing the returned node tree via json_delete.
Thread-safety and errno/diagnostic behavior are unknown.

functions.name: json_encode
functions.description: Serializes a JsonNode tree to a minimal JSON text string (no extra spacing). Use this to produce compact JSON output from an in-memory node. The returned buffer is heap-allocated.
requirements: node must be a valid JsonNode pointer; the structure should be internally consistent (use json_check to verify).
Returned string is heap-allocated; caller must free it using the same allocator used by the library (typically free).
Behavior for nodes with invalid UTF-8 strings/keys is unspecified; strings/keys should be valid UTF-8.

name must be non-NULL.

recurse non-zero to remove within nested subsets (inferred).

functions.name: pr_config_get_id
functions.description: Returns the assigned numeric ID for the provided directive name, or zero if no ID mapping was found. Used to speed lookups by comparing IDs instead of strings.

functions.name: pr_config_set_id

functions.name: get_param_ptr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the parameter/value associated with the named directive in the given set, based on the provided index or occurrence. Useful for accessing directive arguments without copying.

The int parameter likely selects which parameter/occurrence to return (exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: pr_config_merge_down
functions.description: Merges configuration records downward into child contexts according to merge policy and flags, e.g., applying CF_MERGEDOWN or CF_MERGEDOWN_MULTI rules.

functions.name: init_config

functions.name: pr_ctrls_register
functions.signature: int pr_ctrls_register(const module *mod, const char *action, const char *desc, int (*ctrls_cb)(pr_ctrls_t *, int, char **));
functions.description: Registers a control handler callback for the given action with the Controls layer so that clients can invoke it. Returns a handler ID on success, or -1 on error. functions.name: pr_ctrls_unregister
functions.description: Unregisters previously registered control handlers. If mod is NULL, unregisters the specified action for all modules. If action is NULL, unregisters all actions for the specified module. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: If both mod and action are NULL, behavior is to unregister all actions across all modules (implied by the documented rules); exact scope beyond these combinations is not further specified.

functions.name: pr_ctrls_add_arg
functions.description: Appends an argument string to the control object's argument array. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Useful for augmenting or forwarding arguments for a control action.
requirements: ctrl must be a valid, initialized pr_ctrls_t pointer.
ctrls_arg should point to a buffer of length ctrls_arglen; ownership/lifetime must outlive the call (longer persistence is not documented).

functions.name: pr_ctrls_add_response
functions.description: Formats and adds a text response to the control object’s response array (for sending back to the client). Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: ctrl must be a valid, initialized pr_ctrls_t pointer.

Responses added will be available to the requester; flushing/sending is performed by other APIs.

functions.name: pr_ctrls_connect
functions.description: Opens and connects a client control socket to the specified Unix domain socket path. Returns the connected socket file descriptor, or -1 on error. Used by clients such as ftpdctl.

Caller must close the returned fd when done.

functions.name: pr_ctrls_copy_args
functions.description: Copies the argument array from src_ctrl to dest_ctrl. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: src_ctrl and dest_ctrl must be valid pr_ctrls_t objects.
dest_ctrl must be in a state that can accept argument copies (e.g., initialized).

functions.name: pr_ctrls_copy_resps
functions.description: Copies the response array from src_ctrl to dest_ctrl. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: src_ctrl and dest_ctrl must be valid pr_ctrls_t objects.

functions.name: pr_ctrls_flush_response
functions.description: Flushes any responses previously added to the control object out to the client. Intended for use when the control handler will not return (e.g., exiting the process). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (errno EINVAL if ctrl is NULL, EPERM if unable to flush).
requirements: ctrl must be non-NULL (errno EINVAL if NULL).
Only use when the handler will not return, to avoid duplicate or out-of-order responses.

functions.name: pr_ctrls_recv_request

functions.name: pr_ctrls_send_response
functions.signature: int pr_ctrls_send_response(pool *p, int fd, int status, unsigned int argc, char **argv);
functions.description: Sends a control response with the given status and response strings over fd. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: fd must be a connected control socket to the peer expecting the response.

status should be one of the defined PR_CTRLS_STATUS_* values (not strictly required by the signature but implied by API).

functions.description: Accepts a Controls connection on a listening socket. Returns the connected client fd on success, or -1 on error (errno set). If provided, fills in the connecting process’s uid, gid, and pid. max_age specifies the maximum allowed age (seconds) for credentials checking.

functions.name: pr_get_registered_actions
functions.description: Retrieves registered control actions into the provided control object, filtered by flags. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. The exact flag meanings include values like CTRLS_GET_ACTION_ALL, CTRLS_GET_ACTION_ENABLED, CTRLS_GET_DESC.

functions.description: Scans registered controls and frees any that are available for cleanup. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
