functions.name: get_full_cmd
functions.description: Returns the full command string (command plus arguments) for the provided command record.
requirements: cmd_rec* must be valid (non-NULL).
Returned string should be treated as read-only; ownership/lifetime is not documented (likely tied to the cmd_rec pool).

functions.name: init_dirtree
functions.description: Initializes internal data structures used by the dir-tree/configuration subsystem. For internal use only.
requirements: Should be called during server initialization before using dir-tree functions (inferred).
No parameters; may be safe to call once; multiple calls’ behavior is not documented.

functions.name: pr_dirs_dump
functions.description: Development-only helper that dumps directory configuration/state to a caller-provided printf-like output function. Available only when compiled with PR_USE_DEVEL.
requirements: This function is only available when PR_USE_DEVEL is defined at compile time (explicit in header).
First argument must be a valid callback compatible with printf(const char*, ...) to receive the dump output (non-NULL).
xaset_t* must be valid (non-NULL) and represent the directory set to dump.
The char* argument is a NUL-terminated string (e.g., a label/prefix); whether NULL is allowed is not documented.

functions.name: pr_display_fh
functions.signature: int pr_display_fh(struct fh_rec *fh, const char *fs, const char *resp_code, int flags)
functions.description: Reads the contents of the file referred to by the given file handle (fh), considered to be located on the filesystem fs, expands any variables in the file, and sends the resulting lines to the connected client using the provided FTP response code (resp_code). Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error with errno set. Flags may control end-of-message behavior and immediate sending versus queueing.
requirements: fh must be a valid, open file handle (struct fh_rec*) referring to the target file (inferred from parameter type and comment).
fs must name/identify the filesystem on which the file resides; it must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string (explicitly referenced as the filesystem and inferred type semantics).
resp_code must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string representing the response code used when sending lines to the client (explicitly referenced as response code).
flags may include PR_DISPLAY_FL_NO_EOM to avoid ending displayed lines and PR_DISPLAY_FL_SEND_NOW to send lines immediately rather than queueing (explicit per header comments).
Caller must check the return value; on -1, errno is set and should be inspected for the cause (explicit).
Must be invoked in a context where a client session/response mechanism is active so data can be sent to the client (inferred from "send ... to the client" and use of pr_response_send).
Inputs (fh, fs, resp_code) must not be NULL (inferred common requirement for such APIs; NULL behavior is not documented).

functions.name: pr_display_file
functions.signature: int pr_display_file(const char *path, const char *fs, const char *resp_code, int flags)
functions.description: Reads the file at the given path, considered to be located on the filesystem fs, expands any variables in the file, and sends the resulting lines to the connected client using the provided FTP response code (resp_code). Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error with errno set. Flags may control end-of-message behavior and immediate sending versus queueing.
requirements: path must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string naming the file to read (explicitly referenced as the file given by path).
fs must name/identify the filesystem on which the file resides; it must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string (explicitly referenced as the filesystem and inferred type semantics).
resp_code must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string representing the response code used when sending lines to the client (explicitly referenced as response code).
flags may include PR_DISPLAY_FL_NO_EOM to avoid ending displayed lines and PR_DISPLAY_FL_SEND_NOW to send lines immediately rather than queueing (explicit per header comments).
Caller must check the return value; on -1, errno is set and should be inspected for the cause (explicit).
Must be invoked in a context where a client session/response mechanism is active so data can be sent to the client (inferred from "send ... to the client" and use of pr_response_send).
Inputs (path, fs, resp_code) must not be NULL (inferred common requirement for such APIs; NULL behavior is not documented).

functions.name: pr_decode_str
functions.signature: char *pr_decode_str(pool *p, const char *in, size_t inlen, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Translates the input string from the configured encoding into the local charset and returns the translated string. Returns NULL on error. Use when you need server-local charset data from client-provided or externally encoded text. The returned string is allocated from the provided memory pool.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized memory pool from which the returned string will be allocated.
in must point to a readable buffer of at least inlen bytes.
inlen specifies the number of input bytes to translate; how NUL terminators are handled is unknown from this header.
If non-NULL, outlen will receive the number of output bytes; whether it includes a terminating NUL is unknown.
Encoding must be enabled/configured for conversion to occur as intended; behavior if disabled is not specified here.
On error, NULL is returned; callers must check for NULL before using the result.

functions.name: pr_encode_str
functions.signature: char *pr_encode_str(pool *p, const char *in, size_t inlen, size_t *outlen);
functions.description: Translates the input string from the local charset into the currently configured encoding and returns the translated string. Returns NULL on error. Use when you need to send or store text in the configured external encoding.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized memory pool for result allocation.
in must point to a readable buffer of at least inlen bytes.
inlen specifies the number of input bytes to translate; exact handling of NUL terminators is unknown from this header.
If non-NULL, outlen will receive the number of output bytes; whether it includes a terminating NUL is unknown.
Encoding must be enabled/configured for conversion to occur as intended; behavior if disabled is not specified here.
On error, NULL is returned; callers must check for NULL before using the result.

functions.name: pr_encode_disable_encoding
functions.description: Disables runtime use of character encoding (when NLS is supported). Use to force raw/local charset operation without conversions.
requirements: May only have effect if NLS/encoding support is compiled in; otherwise it is a no-op per comment implication.
Callers should be aware that subsequent encode/decode calls will not perform conversions once disabled; exact transition semantics are not detailed.

functions.name: pr_encode_enable_encoding
functions.description: Enables runtime use of character encoding using the specified character set name. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (invalid/unsupported charset or handling failure). Use to activate conversions to/from the named encoding.
requirements: encoding should be a valid, supported character set name; unsupported names cause a -1 return.
Passing NULL or empty strings is not documented; behavior is unknown—callers should avoid NULL to prevent errors.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure and that encoding remains disabled or unchanged.

functions.name: pr_encode_get_policy
functions.description: Returns the current encoding policy bitmask controlling Encode API behavior (e.g., whether to require valid encodings).
requirements: Interpreting the bitmask requires using defined policy flags such as PR_ENCODE_POLICY_FL_REQUIRE_VALID_ENCODING.
Callable at any time; thread-safety or concurrency semantics are not documented.

functions.name: pr_encode_set_policy
functions.description: Sets the encoding policy bitmask controlling Encode API behavior. Return value semantics are not documented in this header (success/failure codes unknown).
requirements: policy should be a bitwise OR of supported flags (e.g., PR_ENCODE_POLICY_FL_REQUIRE_VALID_ENCODING); other bits’ effects are unknown.
Because return codes are not documented here, callers should be prepared for implementation-defined success/failure indications.
Call only with meaningful combinations; invalid combinations’ behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: pr_encode_get_charset
functions.description: Returns a string describing the current charset being used. Intended for informational or diagnostic purposes.
requirements: Return value is a pointer to an internal/static string; lifetime/ownership details are not specified—do not modify the returned string.
Function is read-only and may be called regardless of encoding enablement; exact value when encoding is disabled is not specified.

functions.name: pr_encode_get_local_charset
functions.description: Returns a string describing the local charset (as determined by environment variables and similar).
requirements: Return value is a pointer to an internal/static string; do not modify.
Availability depends on system/environment; exact format and lifetime are not specified.

functions.name: pr_encode_get_encoding
functions.description: Returns a string describing the current character set (or UTF-8) encoding being used. Returns NULL if no encoding is currently in effect.
requirements: Callers must handle a NULL return which indicates no active encoding.
Return value is a pointer to an internal/static string; do not modify the returned data.

functions.name: pr_encode_is_utf8
functions.description: Convenience predicate that returns nonzero (TRUE) if the given encoding name denotes UTF-8, 0 (FALSE) otherwise. Returns -1 on error (e.g., NULL argument). Recognizes multiple UTF-8 name variants.
requirements: codeset must be non-NULL to avoid a -1 error return.
Callers must check for -1 to detect argument/usage errors and not confuse it with FALSE.

functions.name: pr_encode_supports_telnet_iac
functions.description: Returns nonzero (TRUE) if the current encoding supports the Telnet IAC (0xFF) byte unambiguously; returns 0 (FALSE) if the encoding uses 0xFF as a character value (e.g., some CP1251 variants), which may break RFC959 compliance.
requirements: Depends on the currently active encoding; callers should ensure encoding is configured as intended before calling.
Return value is a boolean int; exact nonzero value is implementation-defined.

functions.name: pr_encode_set_charset_encoding
functions.description: Changes both the local charset and the active external encoding in one call. Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not documented in this header.
requirements: charset should be a valid descriptor of the desired local charset; exact accepted formats are unspecified.
encoding should be a valid, supported encoding name; unsupported names likely cause failure (return value semantics unknown).
Callers should check the return value and handle failure; exact success code is not stated here.

functions.name: pr_env_get
functions.description: Returns the value of the environment variable named by key, or NULL if it is not present. Intended for querying the process/module environment within ProFTPD. The pool parameter is used by the implementation (likely for any internal allocations). Ownership of the returned pointer is not explicitly documented; treat it as read-only and do not free it unless you know you own the underlying storage. Usage: call with a valid pool and a variable name to retrieve its current value.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized ProFTPD memory pool pointer with a lifetime suitable for any internal allocations performed by the function (exact allocation behavior is not documented).
key must be non-NULL and should be a valid environment variable name (no '=').
Caller should handle a NULL return indicating the variable is not set.
Do not modify or free the returned string unless you are the owner of the underlying storage (ownership is not explicitly documented).

functions.name: pr_env_set
functions.signature: int pr_env_set(pool *p, const char *key, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets an environment variable named key to value. Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error with errno set. Memory for the strings used in the environment is the caller’s responsibility; if allocating from a memory pool, use a pool with an appropriate lifetime so that the key/value remain valid as long as they may be referenced.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized ProFTPD memory pool pointer.
key must be non-NULL and a valid environment variable name (no '=').
value must be non-NULL; the function sets key to this value.
The memory for key and value must remain valid for as long as the environment may reference them; if allocated from a pool, choose a pool with an appropriate lifetime.
Caller must check the return value; on -1, inspect errno for the failure reason.

functions.name: pr_env_unset
functions.description: Removes any environment variables named key. Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error with errno set.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized ProFTPD memory pool pointer.
key must be non-NULL and a valid environment variable name (no '=').
Caller must check the return value; on -1, inspect errno for the failure reason.

functions.name: pr_error_create
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new error record in the given memory pool, capturing the provided errno value for later explanation/formatting.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized memory pool (pool*).
xerrno should be an errno-style integer captured at the time of failure.
Returned pr_error_t* must be destroyed using pr_error_destroy to avoid leaks (per pool lifecycle).

functions.name: pr_error_destroy
functions.description: Releases any resources associated with the given error record. Intended to be called for error objects created by pr_error_create.
requirements: err must be a pr_error_t* obtained from pr_error_create, allocated from a currently valid pool.
Do not use err after calling this function (dangling pointer).

functions.name: pr_error_get_who
functions.description: Retrieves the UID and GID that were active when the error record was created.
requirements: err must be a valid error object created by pr_error_create.
err_uid and err_gid must be non-NULL pointers to receive the UID/GID.

functions.name: pr_error_set_why
functions.description: Associates a high-level purpose/goal string (the "why") with the error (e.g., the operation intent that failed).
requirements: err must be a valid error object.
goal must be a NUL-terminated string; lifetime must outlive or be copied by the function (copying behavior unknown).

functions.name: pr_error_set_where
functions.signature: int pr_error_set_where(pr_error_t *err, module *m, const char *file, unsigned int lineno);
functions.description: Records the module and source location (file and line) where the error occurred.
requirements: err must be a valid error object.
m should be a valid module pointer (from the ProFTPD module system).
file must be a NUL-terminated filename string.
lineno is a source code line number (non-negative).

functions.name: pr_error_set_what
functions.description: Sets a short description of the specific action or object involved in the error (the "what").
requirements: err must be a valid error object.
what must be a NUL-terminated string; exact ownership/copy semantics are unknown.

functions.name: pr_error_use_details
functions.description: Configures which detail fields are included when formatting errors. The bitmask uses PR_ERROR_DETAILS_USE_* flags.
requirements: use_details must be a bitwise OR of PR_ERROR_DETAILS_USE_NAMES, PR_ERROR_DETAILS_USE_IDS, PR_ERROR_DETAILS_USE_PROTOCOL, PR_ERROR_DETAILS_USE_MODULE, and/or PR_ERROR_DETAILS_USE_FILE.
Caller should use PR_ERROR_DETAILS_DEFAULT if unsure.

functions.name: pr_error_use_formats
functions.description: Selects the allowed output formats (verbosity) for stringifying errors, using PR_ERROR_FORMAT_USE_* flags.
requirements: use_formats must be a bitwise OR of PR_ERROR_FORMAT_USE_DETAILED, PR_ERROR_FORMAT_USE_TERSE, PR_ERROR_FORMAT_USE_MINIMAL.
Caller may use PR_ERROR_FORMAT_DEFAULT as a sensible default.

functions.name: pr_error_strerror
functions.description: Returns a textual representation of the error suitable for logging, honoring the requested format mask.
requirements: err must be a valid error object.
use_format must select one of the configured/allowed formats via PR_ERROR_FORMAT_USE_* flags.
Returned string is const; treat as readonly. Lifetime/ownership is unknown; copy if you need to retain it.

functions.name: pr_error_register_explainer
functions.description: Creates and registers a per-module error explainer, which can provide human-readable explanations for various operations' failures.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized pool.
m must be a valid module pointer.
name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated unique identifier for the explainer within the module/context.

functions.name: pr_error_unregister_explainer
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered error explainer by name for a module.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
m must be a valid module pointer.
name must match a previously registered explainer name.

functions.name: pr_error_use_explainer
functions.description: Selects which registered explainer (by name) should be used for generating explanations.
requirements: p must be a valid pool.
m must be a valid module pointer, typically the owner/consumer of the explainer.
name must reference a registered explainer.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_accept
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_accept(pr_error_t *err, int fd, struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t *addr_len);
functions.description: Populates the error with an explanation for an accept(2) failure using the provided parameters.
requirements: err must be a valid error object whose errno corresponds to the failure.
addr and addr_len should be the same pointers/values used for the failed accept call (non-NULL where required by accept).
fd should be the listening socket descriptor used for accept.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_bind
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_bind(pr_error_t *err, int fd, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addr_len);
functions.description: Explains a bind(2) failure based on the socket and address parameters.
requirements: err must be valid and reflect the errno from the failed bind.
fd is the socket descriptor used for bind.
addr must point to a valid sockaddr structure of length addr_len.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_chdir
functions.description: Explains a chdir(2) failure for the given path.
requirements: err must be valid and contain the errno from the chdir failure.
path must be a NUL-terminated pathname.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_chmod
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_chmod(pr_error_t *err, const char *path, mode_t mode);
functions.description: Explains a chmod(2) failure on a path with the given mode.
requirements: err must be valid with the relevant errno.
path must be a NUL-terminated pathname.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_chown
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_chown(pr_error_t *err, const char *path, uid_t uid, gid_t gid);
functions.description: Explains a chown(2) failure for the path and target ownership.
requirements: err must be valid.
path must be a NUL-terminated pathname.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_chroot
functions.description: Explains a chroot(2) failure to the specified path.
requirements: err must be valid.
path must be a NUL-terminated directory path.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_close
functions.description: Explains a close(2) failure for the given file descriptor.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd should be the same descriptor used in the failed close call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_closedir
functions.description: Explains a closedir(3) failure for the given directory handle.
requirements: err must be valid.
dirh should be the DIR* (passed as void*) originally returned by opendir(3).

functions.name: pr_error_explain_connect
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_connect(pr_error_t *err, int fd, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addr_len);
functions.description: Explains a connect(2) failure for a socket and remote address.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd is the socket descriptor for the failed connect.
addr must point to a sockaddr of length addr_len corresponding to the attempted peer.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fchmod
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_fchmod(pr_error_t *err, int fd, mode_t mode);
functions.description: Explains an fchmod(2) failure on a file descriptor.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd is the descriptor used in the failed fchmod call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fchown
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_fchown(pr_error_t *err, int fd, uid_t uid, gid_t gid);
functions.description: Explains an fchown(2) failure for a file descriptor.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd is the descriptor used in the failed fchown call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fclose
functions.description: Explains an fclose(3) failure for a stream.
requirements: err must be valid.
fh must be a FILE* previously obtained from fopen/fdopen, used in the failed fclose.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fcntl
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_fcntl(pr_error_t *err, int fd, int oper, long arg);
functions.description: Explains an fcntl(2) failure for the given descriptor, command, and argument.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd, oper, and arg should reflect the failed fcntl call parameters.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fdopen
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_fdopen(pr_error_t *err, int fd, const char *mode);
functions.description: Explains an fdopen(3) failure for a file descriptor and mode string.
requirements: err must be valid.
mode must be a NUL-terminated mode string as for fdopen (e.g., "r", "w").

functions.name: pr_error_explain_flock
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_flock(pr_error_t *err, int fd, int oper);
functions.description: Explains a flock(2) failure for the given file descriptor and operation.
requirements: err must be valid.
oper should be the lock operation flags used in the failed flock call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fopen
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_fopen(pr_error_t *err, const char *path, const char *mode);
functions.description: Explains an fopen(3) failure for a path and mode.
requirements: err must be valid.
path and mode must be NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fork
functions.description: Explains a fork(2) failure.
requirements: err must be valid and capture the errno from the failed fork.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fstat
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_fstat(pr_error_t *err, int fd, struct stat *st);
functions.description: Explains an fstat(2) failure for a file descriptor and stat buffer.
requirements: err must be valid.
st must be a valid pointer to a struct stat as used in the failed call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fstatfs
functions.description: Explains an fstatfs(2) failure for a descriptor and filesystem stats buffer.
requirements: err must be valid.
stfs must be a valid pointer to a platform-appropriate statfs structure (type is void* here).

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fstatvfs
functions.description: Explains an fstatvfs(2) failure for a descriptor and vfs stats buffer.
requirements: err must be valid.
stfs must be a valid pointer to a platform-appropriate statvfs structure (type is void* here).

functions.name: pr_error_explain_fsync
functions.description: Explains an fsync(2) failure on a file descriptor.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd must be the same descriptor used in the failed fsync.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_ftruncate
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_ftruncate(pr_error_t *err, int fd, off_t len);
functions.description: Explains an ftruncate(2) failure for a file descriptor and length.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd and len should match the failed ftruncate call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_futimes
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_futimes(pr_error_t *err, int fd, const struct timeval *tvs);
functions.description: Explains a futimes(2) failure for a descriptor and timeval array.
requirements: err must be valid.
tvs must point to a valid array of 2 struct timeval entries (per futimes conventions).

functions.name: pr_error_explain_getaddrinfo
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_getaddrinfo(pr_error_t *err, const char *name, const char *service, const struct addrinfo *hints, struct addrinfo **res);
functions.description: Explains a getaddrinfo(3) failure for the given name/service/hints parameters.
requirements: err must be valid.
name and/or service may be NULL per getaddrinfo rules; when non-NULL they must be NUL-terminated.
hints may be NULL or a valid addrinfo struct pointer.
res is an output parameter from getaddrinfo and may be NULL or a valid pointer.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_gethostbyname
functions.description: Explains a gethostbyname(3) failure for the given hostname.
requirements: err must be valid.
name must be a NUL-terminated hostname string.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_gethostbyname2
functions.description: Explains a gethostbyname2(3) failure for a hostname and address family.
requirements: err must be valid.
name must be a NUL-terminated hostname.
family should be a valid address family (e.g., AF_INET, AF_INET6).

functions.name: pr_error_explain_gethostname
functions.description: Explains a gethostname(2) failure given the buffer and size used.
requirements: err must be valid.
buf must be a valid writable buffer of length sz.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_getnameinfo
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_getnameinfo(pr_error_t *err, const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addr_len, char *host, size_t host_len, char *service, size_t service_len, int flags);
functions.description: Explains a getnameinfo(3) failure for the given socket address, output buffers, and flags.
requirements: err must be valid.
addr must point to a sockaddr of length addr_len.
host/service may be NULL or valid writable buffers with corresponding lengths.
flags should be the same as used for the failed call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_getpeername
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_getpeername(pr_error_t *err, int fd, struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t *addr_len);
functions.description: Explains a getpeername(2) failure for a socket descriptor and output address buffer/length.
requirements: err must be valid.
addr and addr_len must be valid pointers matching the failed call parameters.
fd is the socket descriptor used.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_getrlimit
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_getrlimit(pr_error_t *err, int resource, struct rlimit *rlim);
functions.description: Explains a getrlimit(2) failure for a given resource and rlimit buffer.
requirements: err must be valid.
rlim must be a valid pointer to struct rlimit.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_getsockname
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_getsockname(pr_error_t *err, int fd, struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t *addr_len);
functions.description: Explains a getsockname(2) failure for a socket descriptor and output address buffer/length.
requirements: err must be valid.
addr and addr_len must be valid pointers as used in the failed call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_getsockopt
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_getsockopt(pr_error_t *err, int fd, int level, int option, void *val, socklen_t *valsz);
functions.description: Explains a getsockopt(2) failure given the socket, level/option, and value buffer/size.
requirements: err must be valid.
val must be a valid writable buffer of size *valsz (per failed call).
valsz must be a valid pointer to a socklen_t containing the buffer length.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_lchown
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_lchown(pr_error_t *err, const char *path, uid_t uid, gid_t gid);
functions.description: Explains an lchown(2) failure for the path and desired ownership.
requirements: err must be valid.
path must be a NUL-terminated pathname.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_link
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_link(pr_error_t *err, const char *target_path, const char *link_path);
functions.description: Explains a link(2) failure when creating a hard link from target_path to link_path.
requirements: err must be valid.
target_path and link_path must be NUL-terminated pathnames.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_listen
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_listen(pr_error_t *err, int fd, int backlog);
functions.description: Explains a listen(2) failure for a socket descriptor and backlog.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd must be the socket descriptor used in the failed listen.
backlog should be the same integer used in the call.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_lseek
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_lseek(pr_error_t *err, int fd, off_t offset, int whence);
functions.description: Explains an lseek(2) failure for a descriptor, offset, and whence.
requirements: err must be valid.
fd, offset, and whence must match the failed call parameters.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_lstat
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_lstat(pr_error_t *err, const char *path, struct stat *st);
functions.description: Explains an lstat(2) failure for a path and stat buffer.
requirements: err must be valid.
path must be a NUL-terminated pathname.
st must be a valid struct stat pointer.

functions.name: pr_error_explain_mkdir
functions.signature: int pr_error_explain_mkdir(pr_error_t *err, const char *path, mode_t mode);
functions.description: Explains a mkdir(2) failure for the provided path and mode.
requirements: err must be valid.

functions.description: Registers a handler callback for the named event. The callback will be invoked with event-specific data and the user_data provided here whenever the event is generated. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (errno set). The API stores the pointer to the event name rather than duplicating it, so the event string should have static or otherwise long-lived storage. Typical usage is for modules to subscribe to events they care about and optionally attach per-registration user data.

functions.name: pr_event_unregister
functions.signature: int pr_event_unregister(module *m, const char *event, void (*cb)(const void *, void *));
functions.description: Unregisters previously registered event handlers. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (errno set). Behavior depends on which parameters are non-NULL: if m is non-NULL, only handlers registered by that module are considered; if event is non-NULL, only handlers for that event are considered; if cb is non-NULL, only that specific handler is removed. This allows unregistering a specific handler, all handlers for an event, or all handlers registered by a module.
requirements: If m is non-NULL, the handler(s) being unregistered must have been registered by that module.
If event is non-NULL, only handlers for that event are unregistered; if NULL, all events for the given module may be unregistered.
If cb is non-NULL, the handler being unregistered must match that specific callback.
It is permissible to unregister all handlers for a given event across all modules via pr_event_unregister(NULL, event_name, NULL).
It is permissible to unregister all handlers for a module via pr_event_unregister(&my_module, NULL, NULL).
On return -1, callers should check errno for the error cause.

functions.name: glob
functions.signature: int glob(const char* __pattern, int __flags, int (*__errfunc)(const char*, int), glob_t* __pglob);
functions.description: Perform pathname expansion (globbing) for the pattern string and store results in the glob_t pointed to by __pglob. The behavior is controlled by the bitmask __flags (e.g., GLOB_ERR, GLOB_MARK, GLOB_NOSORT, GLOB_DOOFFS, GLOB_NOCHECK, GLOB_APPEND, GLOB_NOESCAPE, GLOB_PERIOD, and, when available under feature macros, GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC, GLOB_BRACE, GLOB_NOMAGIC, GLOB_TILDE, GLOB_ONLYDIR, GLOB_TILDE_CHECK). On directory read/open errors, if __errfunc is non-NULL it is called with the pathname and errno; a nonzero return from __errfunc causes glob to abort with GLOB_ABORTED. On success returns 0 and populates __pglob->gl_pathv and counts; on failure returns one of GLOB_NOSPACE, GLOB_ABORTED, GLOB_NOMATCH, or GLOB_NOSYS. If GLOB_NOCHECK is set and no matches are found, the pattern itself is returned as a single result and the function returns 0. Typical usage: initialize glob_t, call glob with desired flags, then free resources with globfree.
requirements: __pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string pointer (non-NULL).

__flags is a bitmask; only the bits documented for glob are valid (platform/feature-macro dependent): GLOB_ERR, GLOB_MARK, GLOB_NOSORT, GLOB_DOOFFS, GLOB_NOCHECK, GLOB_APPEND, GLOB_NOESCAPE, GLOB_PERIOD, and possibly GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC, GLOB_BRACE, GLOB_NOMAGIC, GLOB_TILDE, GLOB_ONLYDIR, GLOB_TILDE_CHECK.
__pglob must be non-NULL and point to a glob_t structure.
If __flags includes GLOB_DOOFFS, the caller must set __pglob->gl_offs before calling; glob will reserve that many NULL slots at the start of gl_pathv.
If __flags includes GLOB_APPEND, __pglob must already contain the results of a previous successful glob call (not yet freed); glob will append new results to those existing entries.

If __flags includes GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC, the following function pointers in __pglob must be set to valid implementations prior to the call: gl_opendir(const char*), gl_readdir(void*), gl_closedir(void*), gl_lstat(const char*, struct stat*), and gl_stat(const char*, struct stat*).
__errfunc may be NULL. If non-NULL, it must be callable with (const char* path, int err) and should return 0 to ignore the error or nonzero to cause glob to abort with GLOB_ABORTED.
On success or on any return that allocated memory in __pglob (including the GLOB_NOCHECK case), the caller must later call globfree(__pglob) to release resources.
Do not use or free the strings in __pglob->gl_pathv individually; treat them as owned by the glob result and release them via globfree.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not guaranteed by this declaration; callers must avoid sharing/modifying the same glob_t concurrently across threads.

functions.name: globfree
functions.description: Release all storage allocated in the glob_t structure by a previous call to glob. After returning, the contents of *__pglob (including gl_pathv and gl_pathc) are no longer valid.
requirements: __pglob must be non-NULL and must point to a glob_t that was previously initialized by a call to glob (including the GLOB_NOCHECK case that produced an allocated result).
Do not use __pglob->gl_pathv or any of its elements after calling globfree.
Safe to call exactly once for a given successful glob result; calling globfree multiple times on the same result leads to undefined behavior.
__pglob must not be used concurrently from multiple threads while calling globfree.

functions.name: glob64
functions.signature: int glob64(const char* __pattern, int __flags, int (*__errfunc)(const char*, int), glob64_t* __pglob);
functions.description: Large-file variant of glob that fills a glob64_t and uses 64-bit stat/dirent types when available. Behavior, flags, and error handling are the same as glob, but the auxiliary callbacks (when GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC is used) take struct stat64/dirent64 types. Available when _LARGEFILE64_SOURCE is defined.
requirements: Available only when _LARGEFILE64_SOURCE is defined at compile time.
__pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string pointer (non-NULL).
__flags is a bitmask of the same GLOB_* flags applicable to glob on this platform.
__pglob must be non-NULL and point to a glob64_t structure.
If __flags includes GLOB_DOOFFS, set __pglob->gl_offs before calling.
If __flags includes GLOB_APPEND, __pglob must already contain results from a prior successful glob64 call that have not been freed.

If __flags includes GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC, the following function pointers in __pglob must be set before the call: gl_opendir(const char*), gl_readdir(void* or struct dirent64* returning function depending on feature), gl_closedir(void*), gl_lstat(const char*, struct stat64*), and gl_stat(const char*, struct stat64*).
__errfunc may be NULL; if non-NULL its nonzero return forces GLOB_ABORTED.
On success or any case that allocates memory, the caller must later call globfree64(__pglob).

functions.name: globfree64
functions.description: Free storage allocated in a glob64_t by a previous glob64 call. After the call, the contents of *__pglob are invalid.
requirements: Available only when _LARGEFILE64_SOURCE is defined at compile time.
__pglob must be non-NULL and must point to a glob64_t previously initialized by glob64.
Call exactly once per successful glob64 result; do not access gl_pathv or its elements after freeing.
Do not call concurrently on the same glob64_t from multiple threads.

functions.name: glob_pattern_p
functions.description: Return nonzero if the pattern contains any glob metacharacters. If __quote is nonzero, backslashes are treated as quoting characters and can escape metacharacters; if zero, backslashes do not quote. This is a GNU extension commonly used to detect whether a string needs globbing.
requirements: Available only when _GNU_SOURCE is defined at compile time.
__pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string pointer (non-NULL).
__quote is an int treated as boolean: nonzero enables backslash-quoting, zero disables it.

functions.name: tpl_fatal
functions.description: Default fatal-error handler hook for the tpl library. Intended to log a formatted error message (printf-style) and typically abort or terminate the process (behavior inferred from the name "fatal"). Use this only as a callback/hook replacement or to emit an unrecoverable error message.
requirements: fmt should be a valid, null-terminated C format string (printf-style).
The variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.
Behavior on return is unknown; typical fatal handlers may not return (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_map
functions.description: Creates (maps) a tpl schema/tree from a format string and associated arguments. The resulting tpl_node describes how to pack/unpack data according to the format. Use the returned node with tpl_pack/tpl_unpack and free it with tpl_free when done.
requirements: fmt must be a valid, null-terminated format string understood by tpl (exact grammar not provided here).
The variadic arguments must supply addresses/types matching fmt (inferred from typical tpl usage).
The returned tpl_node* must be freed with tpl_free to avoid leaks.
All pointers provided via variadic arguments must remain valid for the lifetime of the tpl_node (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_free
functions.description: Frees a tpl map previously created by tpl_map, releasing all associated resources.
requirements: r should be a tpl_node* previously returned by tpl_map (or NULL-safe behavior is unknown).
Do not call tpl_free more than once on the same tpl_node* (double-free is undefined, inferred).
Ensure no concurrent use of r is in progress when freeing (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_pack
functions.description: Packs (serializes into the tpl image buffer) the i-th packable element defined in the tpl map r. Typically used after setting source data bound via tpl_map.
requirements: r must be a valid tpl_node* created by tpl_map.
i selects the packable element index; it must refer to a valid packable (exact bounds unknown).
Return value semantics (0/negative for error) are not documented here; caller must check the return value for success/failure (inferred).
Data addresses referenced by r must be initialized and valid before calling (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_unpack
functions.description: Unpacks (deserializes from the currently loaded tpl image) the i-th packable element into the data addresses bound in the tpl map r.
requirements: r must be a valid tpl_node* created by tpl_map, with matching format to the loaded image.
tpl_load must have been called successfully on r before unpacking (inferred from typical workflow).
i must refer to a valid packable index within r (exact bounds unknown).
Caller must check the return value to detect errors (semantics not documented here).
Destination memory referenced by r must be writable and sufficiently sized (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_dump
functions.description: Serializes (dumps) the tpl map r into a destination specified by mode and variadic parameters. Destinations may include memory, file path, or file descriptor as suggested by available flags.
requirements: r must be a valid tpl_node* created by tpl_map and populated via tpl_pack as needed (inferred).

mode must be a valid combination of dump flags (e.g., TPL_FILE, TPL_MEM, TPL_FD, TPL_PREALLOCD, TPL_EXCESS_OK, TPL_UFREE, TPL_DATAPEEK, TPL_FXLENS, TPL_GETSIZE). Exact combinations and constraints are not documented here.
The variadic arguments must match the destination implied by mode (e.g., pointer/size for memory, filename or fd for file; exact signatures are not specified here).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure (semantics not documented here).
If using memory destinations, provided buffers must be valid and sized appropriately unless using modes that allocate internally (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_load
functions.description: Associates a data source (memory, file, or descriptor depending on mode) with the tpl map r to prepare for unpacking. Typically called before tpl_unpack.
requirements: r must be a valid tpl_node* created by tpl_map and formatted to match the incoming data (inferred).
mode must be a valid source flag combination (e.g., TPL_FILE, TPL_MEM, TPL_FD). Exact requirements are not specified here.
The variadic arguments must match the source implied by mode (e.g., pointer/size, filename, or fd; exact signatures are not specified here).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure (semantics not documented here).
The source data must remain available and unchanged for the lifetime of unpack operations (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_Alen
functions.description: Returns the array length of the i-th packable element in the tpl map r. Useful for determining sizes of array-type fields described by the format.
requirements: r must be a valid tpl_node* created by tpl_map.
i must refer to a valid packable index within r (exact bounds unknown).
Return value interpretation for errors (e.g., negative) is not documented here; caller should check for non-negative results (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_peek
functions.description: Provides a quick peek at the format string or metadata based on mode. Returns a pointer to a character buffer; the exact meaning depends on mode. Details are not documented in this header.
requirements: mode must be a valid value accepted by tpl_peek; specific modes and their varargs are not documented here.
The variadic arguments must match the chosen mode’s expected parameters (unknown specifics).
The lifetime/ownership of the returned char* is unspecified; caller must not assume it is persistent or modifiable (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_gather
functions.description: Asynchronously or incrementally gathers tpl images from a stream or memory, depending on mode. Supports blocking, non-blocking, or memory modes as suggested by TPL_GATHER_BLOCKING, TPL_GATHER_NONBLOCKING, and TPL_GATHER_MEM. Typically used with a buffer/state (tpl_gather_t) and an optional callback (tpl_gather_cb) when a full image is assembled.
requirements: mode must be one of TPL_GATHER_BLOCKING, TPL_GATHER_NONBLOCKING, or TPL_GATHER_MEM.
The variadic arguments must correspond to the selected mode (e.g., pointers to tpl_gather_t, data sources, and optional tpl_gather_cb; exact signatures are not specified here).
Caller must check the return value for success or completion indications (semantics not documented here).
Any buffers or state structures passed must remain valid for the duration of the gather operation (inferred).

functions.name: tpl_jot
functions.description: Quickly writes a simple tpl image according to mode and variadic parameters. Intended as a convenience for simple one-off serialization to memory or file. Exact parameter forms depend on mode.
requirements: mode must be a valid target selector compatible with tpl_jot (not documented here).
The variadic arguments must match the destination implied by mode (unknown specifics).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure (semantics not documented here).

functions.name: pr_help_add

functions.name: pr_inet_reverse_dns

functions.name: pr_inet_getservport
functions.signature: int pr_inet_getservport(pool *, const char *, const char *);

functions.name: pr_inet_getaddr

functions.name: pr_inet_copy_conn
functions.description: Creates a copy/clone of a connection object into the specified pool. Useful for duplicating connection state for child processes or sessions.

functions.name: pr_inet_create_conn
functions.signature: conn_t *pr_inet_create_conn(pool *p, int fd, const pr_netaddr_t *bind_addr, int port, int retry_bind);

functions.name: pr_inet_create_conn2
functions.signature: conn_t *pr_inet_create_conn2(pool *p, int fd, const pr_netaddr_t *bind_addr, int port, int flags);
functions.description: Creates a new conn_t similar to pr_inet_create_conn, with a bitmask flags parameter to alter behavior (e.g., retry bind, error logging). Returns a conn_t* or NULL.

port must be 0-65535.

Caller must validate the return and handle allocation/bind errors.

functions.name: pr_inet_create_conn_portrange
functions.signature: conn_t *pr_inet_create_conn_portrange(pool *p, const pr_netaddr_t *bind_addr, int min_port, int max_port);
functions.description: Creates a new conn_t bound to bind_addr using an available port within [min_port, max_port]. Returns the created connection or NULL on failure.
requirements: p must be valid.
bind_addr may be NULL to use any/local address.
min_port and max_port must be within 1-65535 and min_port <= max_port.

functions.name: pr_inet_close
functions.description: Closes the connection associated with the given conn_t, releasing its socket descriptors/streams and related resources back to the provided pool context.
requirements: pool* must be valid.
conn_t* must be non-NULL and previously created/initialized by the inet API.
After calling, the conn_t should not be used except as documented by the library (likely invalid).

functions.name: pr_inet_lingering_abort
functions.description: Aborts a lingering close on a connection, or performs an abortive close with a configurable linger period. The long parameter is a timeout/interval; units are not documented.

conn_t* must be a valid open connection.
The timeout parameter must be >= 0; exact units (seconds/milliseconds) are unknown from this header.
Should only be called when a connection is being shut down/aborted.

functions.name: pr_inet_lingering_close
functions.description: Performs a graceful lingering close on the connection, allowing pending data to be transmitted for up to the specified timeout before closing. Units of the long parameter are unspecified in this header.
requirements: pool* must be valid.
conn_t* must be a valid open connection.

Caller should not reuse the conn_t for I/O after initiating lingering close.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_default_family
functions.description: Sets the default address family (e.g., AF_INET or AF_INET6) used by subsequent inet operations that do not explicitly specify a family. Returns status code.
requirements: pool* must be valid.

Caller must check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_async
functions.description: Configures the connection's socket(s) for asynchronous (non-blocking) I/O and adjusts associated internal streams. Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.
requirements: pool* must be valid.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_block
functions.description: Sets the connection's socket(s) into blocking mode. Returns status code.
requirements: pool* must be valid.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_nonblock
functions.description: Sets the connection's socket(s) into non-blocking mode. Returns status code.
requirements: pool* must be valid.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_proto_cork

requirements: First int must be a valid socket file descriptor.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_proto_keepalive
functions.description: Configures TCP keepalive on the connection using the provided tcp_keepalive settings. Returns status code.

struct tcp_keepalive* must be non-NULL and populated per platform expectations (intervals, idle, probes).

functions.name: pr_inet_set_proto_nodelay

functions.name: pr_inet_set_proto_opts

functions.description: Sets multiple protocol-level options on the connection (e.g., buffer sizes, low-water marks). Specific options are not documented here. Returns status code.
requirements: pool* must be valid.
conn_t* must be a valid, open connection.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_reuse_port
functions.description: Sets the SO_REUSEPORT option (if supported) on the connection's socket. Returns status code indicating success/failure.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_socket_opts
functions.signature: int pr_inet_set_socket_opts(pool *, conn_t *, int, int, struct tcp_keepalive *);

requirements: pool* must be valid.
conn_t* must be a valid, open connection.
The integer parameters must be within valid ranges for their respective options; exact meanings are not documented here.
If tcp_keepalive* is non-NULL, it must point to a properly initialized structure compatible with the platform.

functions.name: pr_inet_set_socket_opts2
functions.signature: int pr_inet_set_socket_opts2(pool *, conn_t *, int, int, struct tcp_keepalive *, int);
functions.description: Like pr_inet_set_socket_opts but with an additional flags/int parameter for extended control. Returns status code.

functions.name: pr_inet_resetlisten

Caller must check the return value and handle failures.

functions.name: pr_inet_accept_nowait
functions.description: Attempts a non-blocking accept on the listening connection. Returns a status code; exact return conventions (e.g., 0, >0 fd, or -1 on error) are not specified in this header.
requirements: pool* must be valid.
conn_t* must be in listen mode with a valid listening socket.
Caller must handle the non-blocking case (e.g., EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK) and check the return value semantics as defined by the implementation.

functions.name: pr_inet_connect
functions.signature: int pr_inet_connect(pool *, conn_t *, const pr_netaddr_t *, int);
functions.description: Connects the connection's socket to the specified remote address and port, blocking until completion. Returns status code.
requirements: pool* must be valid.
conn_t* must be a valid connection with a socket (created/bound as appropriate).
The remote pr_netaddr_t* must be non-NULL and valid.

functions.description: Initiates a non-blocking connect to the specified remote address and port. Returns immediately with a status code indicating progress or failure.
