functions.description: Initializes a ctrls_acl_t object to a known default state for subsequent configuration (e.g., by setting user/group ACLs). Call before using the ACL in checks.
requirements: acl must be a non-NULL pointer to writable memory
Caller should not assume prior contents are preserved; the structure will be reset to defaults
After initialization, configure specific user/group ACLs as needed before using in checks

functions.name: pr_ctrls_parse_acl
functions.description: Parses a comma-separated list of names from an ACL configuration string into a NULL-terminated array of strings allocated from acl_pool. Use the returned array to supply name lists to other ACL configuration functions.
requirements: acl_pool must be a valid memory pool for allocations
acl_text should be a null-terminated string containing a comma-separated list (may be empty)
The returned array and its strings are allocated from acl_pool and must not be freed manually; they remain valid while acl_pool lives
The returned array is NULL-terminated; callers must iterate until a NULL entry

functions.name: pr_ctrls_set_group_acl
functions.signature: int pr_ctrls_set_group_acl(pool *, ctrls_group_acl_t *, const char *, char *);
functions.description: Configures a ctrls_group_acl_t from textual inputs (e.g., allow/deny and a list of group names/IDs). Uses the provided pool for any allocations. The list parameter is mutable and may be tokenized in-place.
requirements: pool* must be a valid allocation pool
ctrls_group_acl_t* must be a valid, writable ACL structure (initialized or ready to be initialized)
The const char* parameter denotes configuration (e.g., whether to allow or deny); exact accepted values are not specified here (unknown)
The char* list must point to a writable, null-terminated buffer (not a string literal), as the function may modify it during parsing
On success, ctrls_group_acl_t.gids and ngids will reflect the configured entries; callers should not free memory directly but rely on the pool lifecycle
Return value semantics (0 vs non-zero) are not documented here; callers should check for success/failure per the library’s conventions (unknown)

functions.name: pr_ctrls_set_user_acl
functions.signature: int pr_ctrls_set_user_acl(pool *, ctrls_user_acl_t *, const char *, char *);
functions.description: Configures a ctrls_user_acl_t from textual inputs (e.g., allow/deny and a list of user names/IDs). Uses the provided pool for any allocations. The list parameter is mutable and may be tokenized in-place.
requirements: pool* must be a valid allocation pool
ctrls_user_acl_t* must be a valid, writable ACL structure (initialized or ready to be initialized)
The const char* parameter denotes configuration (e.g., whether to allow or deny); exact accepted values are not specified here (unknown)
The char* list must point to a writable, null-terminated buffer (not a string literal), as the function may modify it during parsing
On success, ctrls_user_acl_t.uids and nuids will reflect the configured entries; callers should not free memory directly but rely on the pool lifecycle
Return value semantics (0 vs non-zero) are not documented here; callers should check for success/failure per the library’s conventions (unknown)

functions.name: pr_ctrls_set_module_acls
functions.signature: char *pr_ctrls_set_module_acls(ctrls_acttab_t *ctrls_acttab, pool *acl_pool, char **actions, const char *allow, const char *type, char *list);
functions.description: Configures the ACLs for the actions implemented by a Controls module. The actions array identifies which actions to configure, allow/type control the ACL semantics, and list provides the user/group names. Returns, on error, the offending/unknown action name; otherwise likely NULL.
requirements: ctrls_acttab must point to the module’s action table entries to be configured
acl_pool must be a valid pool for any allocations made during configuration
actions must be a valid, NULL-terminated array of action name strings (inferred from typical ProFTPD patterns)
allow should be a valid token indicating whether to allow or deny (exact accepted values unspecified here; unknown)
type should identify the ACL type being configured (e.g., user or group; exact values unspecified here; unknown)
list must be a writable, null-terminated buffer containing a comma-separated list; it may be modified during parsing
On error, the function returns a pointer to the offending/unknown action name; callers must check the return value before assuming success

functions.name: pr_ctrls_set_module_acls2
functions.signature: int pr_ctrls_set_module_acls2(ctrls_acttab_t *ctrls_acttab, pool *acl_pool, char **actions, const char *allow, const char *type, char *list, const char **bad_action);
functions.description: Configures the ACLs for a module’s actions (like pr_ctrls_set_module_acls), but reports failures via a return code and by setting bad_action to the offending/unknown action name.
requirements: ctrls_acttab must point to the module’s action table entries to be configured
acl_pool must be a valid pool for allocations
actions must be a valid, NULL-terminated array of action name strings (inferred)
allow should be a valid allow/deny token (exact accepted values unknown)
type should denote the ACL type (e.g., user/group; exact values unknown)
list must be a writable, null-terminated buffer that may be modified during parsing
bad_action, if non-NULL, will be set on error to point to the offending action name; its lifetime follows the underlying storage (do not free)
Return code semantics are not specified here; callers must check the int return and bad_action to detect errors (unknown exact convention)

functions.name: pr_ctrls_unregister_module_actions
functions.description: Unregisters a module’s control actions according to the configured list. On error, returns the offending/unknown action name; otherwise likely NULL.
requirements: ctrls_acttab must reference the module’s action table
actions must be a valid, NULL-terminated array of action names to unregister (inferred)
mod must be a valid pointer to the module whose actions are being unregistered
On error, return value is a pointer to the offending action name; callers must check the return value

functions.name: pr_ctrls_unregister_module_actions2
functions.description: Unregisters a module’s control actions, reporting failures via return code and setting bad_action to the offending/unknown action name on error.
requirements: ctrls_acttab must reference the module’s action table
actions must be a valid, NULL-terminated array of action names to unregister (inferred)
mod must be a valid module pointer
bad_action, if non-NULL, will be set on error to identify the offending action; do not free the returned pointer
Return code semantics are not specified here; callers must check the int return and bad_action for errors (unknown exact convention)

functions.name: pr_ctrls_set_logfd
functions.description: Sets the file descriptor that the Controls API uses for logging (e.g., for pr_ctrls_log).
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor suitable for writing
The file descriptor should remain open and writable for the duration of logging
Callers should check the return value to ensure the log destination was successfully set (exact return convention unknown)

functions.name: pr_ctrls_log
functions.description: Writes a formatted log message to the mod_ctrls-specific log, using printf-style formatting. Intended for module code to report events, tagging messages with the module_version string.
requirements: module_version must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string identifying the module/version
fmt must be a non-NULL printf-style format string
The variadic arguments must match the fmt specifiers (GCC format checking is enabled)
A logging destination should be configured (e.g., via pr_ctrls_set_logfd) before calling to ensure messages are emitted (recommended; exact requirement unknown)
Return value semantics (e.g., bytes written or status) are not specified; callers should check for negative/error values per implementation (unknown)

functions.name: command_exists
functions.description: Checks whether a command name is registered/known to the server’s command table. Returns a nonzero value if the command exists, zero otherwise. Intended for use by modules or core code to gate behavior based on command availability.
requirements: command must be a valid, null-terminated string
Behavior for NULL or empty strings is unspecified; pass a non-NULL pointer

functions.name: modules_init
functions.description: Initializes the module subsystem prior to use (e.g., loading built-in tables, preparing internal lists). Should be called before other module-management functions.
requirements: Should be called before any other module enumeration/loading/unloading routines
Should be called exactly once during process initialization; reinitialization behavior is unspecified
Return value semantics are not documented here; caller must check and handle nonzero/negative values as failure as per project conventions

functions.name: modules_list
functions.description: Lists currently available/loaded modules using the default listing mechanism/log sink. flags controls output details (e.g., show version or static modules).
requirements: flags is a bitmask of PR_MODULES_LIST_FL_SHOW_VERSION (0x00001) and PR_MODULES_LIST_FL_SHOW_STATIC (0x00002); it may be 0 for default listing
No return value; caller should not assume synchronous output destination beyond default project behavior

functions.name: modules_list2
functions.description: Lists modules using a caller-provided printf-like callback. Enables directing the listing to custom sinks (buffers, logs, etc.).
requirements: listf must be a valid function pointer compatible with int f(const char*, ...) that accepts printf-style format strings and arguments
listf must be safe to call multiple times and may be invoked for multiple lines
flags is a bitmask of PR_MODULES_LIST_FL_SHOW_VERSION (0x00001) and PR_MODULES_LIST_FL_SHOW_STATIC (0x00002); it may be 0
Passing NULL for listf is invalid/unspecified; provide a non-NULL callback

functions.name: modules_session_init
functions.description: Per-session initialization hook for the module subsystem (e.g., to let modules perform session-scoped setup).
requirements: Call after global modules_init() and when a session context exists
Return value semantics are not documented here; caller should test for failure per project conventions

functions.name: pr_module_exists
functions.description: Checks whether a module with the given name is present/registered. Returns nonzero if found, zero otherwise.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated string naming the module
Behavior for NULL or empty strings is unspecified; pass a non-NULL pointer

functions.name: pr_module_get
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the module structure for the named module if present, otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated string
Caller must check for NULL return before dereferencing the result

functions.name: pr_module_load
functions.description: Loads/activates the given module, wiring up its tables and initialization as needed.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer to a module structure
The module should not already be loaded; behavior on re-loading is unspecified
Caller must check the return value and handle errors per project conventions

functions.name: pr_module_unload
functions.description: Unloads/deactivates the given module, tearing down associated resources.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer to a module structure that has been previously loaded
After successful unload, the module pointer must not be used for calls that require a loaded module
Caller must check the return value and handle errors per project conventions

functions.name: pr_module_load_authtab
functions.description: Loads the authentication handler table (authtable) from the specified module.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer to a module structure
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact codes are not documented here

functions.name: pr_module_load_cmdtab
functions.description: Loads the command handler table (cmdtable) from the specified module.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer to a module structure
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact codes are not documented here

functions.name: pr_module_load_conftab
functions.description: Loads the configuration directive table (conftable) from the specified module.
requirements: m must be a valid pointer to a module structure
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact codes are not documented here

functions.name: pr_module_call
functions.description: Invokes the specified module handler with the provided cmd_rec, returning the handler’s modret_t result. Allows dispatch to a specific module or, depending on implementation, to a sentinel such as ANY_MODULE.
requirements: handler must be a valid function pointer of type modret_t *(*)(cmd_rec *)
cmd must point to a valid command record expected by the handler
m must be a valid module pointer or a documented sentinel (ANY_MODULE); exact behavior for NULL or special values is not specified here
Caller must check the returned modret_t*: NULL indicates PR_DECLINED per macros; non-NULL with mr_error set indicates error

functions.name: set_auth_check
functions.description: Registers the authentication-check callback used by the command authorization path. Stores the function pointer in the global cmd_auth_chk.
requirements: ck should be a function pointer of type int (*)(cmd_rec *). Passing NULL is not documented here; behavior may clear or disable the check but is unspecified
The callback must be safe to call during command processing for any relevant commands

functions.name: mod_create_ret
functions.signature: modret_t *mod_create_ret(cmd_rec *cmd, unsigned char is_error, const char *numeric, const char *message);
functions.description: Creates a modret_t return object for a module handler, optionally marking it as an error and setting an FTP-style numeric code and message. Intended for use inside module handler functions.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer to the current cmd_rec
is_error is treated as boolean: 0 for handled/success, nonzero for error
numeric may be NULL or a valid null-terminated string representing a numeric code
message may be NULL or a valid null-terminated string with a text message
Primarily intended for use within module handler contexts

functions.name: mod_create_error
functions.description: Creates a modret_t representing an error condition for a module handler using a numeric error indicator (often an errno or protocol code).
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer to the current cmd_rec
errnum is an integer error indicator; exact interpretation is not documented here
Caller should treat the returned modret_t as an error (mr_error nonzero)

functions.name: mod_create_data
functions.description: Creates a modret_t carrying an auxiliary data payload for module handlers. Useful for passing additional handler-specific data back to the caller.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer to the current cmd_rec
data may be NULL or a valid pointer; semantics of the data pointer are handler-specific and not defined here
Ownership/lifetime of data is unspecified; caller and callee must agree on management

functions.name: core_chgrp
functions.signature: int core_chgrp(cmd_rec *cmd, const char *path, uid_t uid, gid_t gid);
functions.description: Core helper to change ownership/group of a filesystem object associated with a command. Based on the name, it likely adjusts group (and possibly user) ownership of path. Implemented in mod_core.c. Return value semantics are not specified here.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer to the current cmd_rec
path must be a valid, null-terminated pathname
uid and gid must be valid identifiers for the target system; exact accepted ranges are system-defined
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact semantics (0/-1/etc.) are not documented here

functions.name: core_chmod
functions.signature: int core_chmod(cmd_rec *cmd, const char *path, mode_t mode);
functions.description: Core helper to change permissions (mode) of a filesystem object associated with a command. Implemented in mod_core.c. Return value semantics are not specified here.
requirements: cmd must be a valid pointer to the current cmd_rec
path must be a valid, null-terminated pathname
mode must be a valid mode_t bitmask per the target system (e.g., permission bits)
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact semantics (0/-1/etc.) are not documented here

functions.name: pr_netacl_create
functions.description: Parses the provided C string into a network ACL (pr_netacl_t) allocated from the given memory pool. On parse failure, returns NULL and sets errno. Intended for constructing ACLs (e.g., IP/DNS match expressions) from configuration or user input.
requirements: The pool * argument must be a valid, initialized memory pool suitable for allocating the ACL object.
The char * argument must be a valid, NUL-terminated C string containing the ACL expression to parse.
Because the parameter type is char * (not const), callers should not pass string literals; the implementation may modify the buffer during parsing.
On error, the function returns NULL and sets errno; callers must check for NULL and handle errno accordingly.

functions.name: pr_netacl_dup
functions.description: Creates and returns a duplicate of the given netacl, allocating the copy from the specified pool. Use to clone an existing ACL into a different pool or for independent lifetime management.
requirements: The pool * argument must be a valid, initialized memory pool suitable for allocations.
The const pr_netacl_t * argument must point to a valid, initialized ACL object to duplicate.
On failure, the function may return NULL (behavior not explicitly documented here); callers should be prepared to handle a NULL result if duplication cannot be performed.

functions.name: pr_netacl_match
functions.description: Tests whether the provided network address matches the given ACL. Returns 1 if explicitly matched, -1 if explicitly not matched (e.g., ACL like "none"), and 0 if there is no match. Useful for authorization or filtering decisions.
requirements: The const pr_netacl_t * argument must be a valid, initialized ACL object.
The const pr_netaddr_t * argument must be a valid, initialized network address object.
Callers must handle all three return values: 1 (match), 0 (no match), and -1 (explicit non-match). Do not treat -1 as an error; it indicates an explicit negative match per ACL semantics.
No errno behavior is specified for this function; return values encode the match result.

functions.name: pr_netacl_get_negated
functions.description: Reports whether the ACL is negated. Returns TRUE if negated, FALSE if not, and -1 on error (errno set). Negated ACLs invert their match semantics.
requirements: The const pr_netacl_t * argument must be a valid, initialized ACL object.
Callers must handle three outcomes: TRUE (nonzero), FALSE (zero), and -1 for error.
If the function returns -1, callers must read errno to determine the error cause.

functions.name: pr_netacl_get_type
functions.description: Returns the ACL's type enumeration (e.g., PR_NETACL_TYPE_ALL, PR_NETACL_TYPE_IPMASK, PR_NETACL_TYPE_DNSGLOB). Use to branch logic based on ACL kind.
requirements: The const pr_netacl_t * argument must be a valid, initialized ACL object.
Callers must be prepared to handle any value of pr_netacl_type_t defined in this header.
No explicit error/errno semantics are documented for this function.

functions.name: pr_netacl_get_str
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the given ACL. The returned string is allocated from the provided pool and remains valid per that pool's lifetime.
requirements: The pool *p must be a valid, initialized memory pool used for the returned string's storage.
The const pr_netacl_t *acl must be a valid, initialized ACL object.
Callers must not modify or free the returned string directly; its lifetime is managed by the pool.
On failure, behavior is not explicitly documented; callers should defensively check for a NULL return.

functions.name: pr_netacl_get_str2
functions.signature: const char *pr_netacl_get_str2(pool *p, const pr_netacl_t *acl, int flags);
functions.description: Returns a string describing the ACL, with formatting controlled by flags (e.g., PR_NETACL_FL_STR_NO_DESC to suppress extra description). The string is allocated from the provided pool.
requirements: The pool *p must be a valid, initialized memory pool used for the returned string's storage.
The const pr_netacl_t *acl must be a valid, initialized ACL object.
The flags argument must be a valid bitmask; supported bits include PR_NETACL_FL_STR_NO_DESC (0x0001). Unknown flags behavior is unspecified and should be avoided.
Callers must not modify or free the returned string directly; its lifetime is managed by the pool.
On failure, behavior is not explicitly documented; callers should defensively check for a NULL return.

functions.name: pr_getaddrinfo
functions.signature: int pr_getaddrinfo(const char *, const char *, const struct addrinfo *, struct addrinfo **);
functions.description: Wrapper for getaddrinfo(3). Resolves a host/service name pair into one or more addrinfo records. Depending on build-time defines it may map directly to system getaddrinfo. Use ai_hints to constrain results; results are returned as a linked list via the out-parameter.
requirements: First argument (node/host) may be NULL or a hostname/address string as per getaddrinfo(3) semantics; second argument (service) may be NULL or service/port string.
If ai_hints is non-NULL, its ai_family/ai_socktype/ai_protocol/ai_flags must contain valid values from AF_*, SOCK_*, IPPROTO_*, AI_*.
The result pointer must be non-NULL and will receive an allocated list that must later be freed using pr_freeaddrinfo().
Return value should be checked: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates an EAI_* error; EAI_SYSTEM implies errno is set.

functions.name: pr_freeaddrinfo
functions.description: Wrapper for freeaddrinfo(3). Frees a list of addrinfo structures previously obtained via pr_getaddrinfo.
requirements: Argument must be either NULL (no-op) or a pointer previously returned by pr_getaddrinfo.
Do not use the pointer after calling this function (use-after-free).

functions.name: pr_getnameinfo
functions.signature: int pr_getnameinfo(const struct sockaddr *, socklen_t, char *, size_t, char *, size_t, int);
functions.description: Wrapper for getnameinfo(3). Converts a socket address to its host and/or service name strings into supplied buffers, controlled by flags.
requirements: sockaddr pointer must be a valid address with correct length for its family (socklen_t len).
host buffer pointer and length may be NULL/0 if host resolution not desired; same for service buffer/length.
flags must be valid NI_* bitmask values (e.g., NI_NUMERICHOST, NI_NUMERICSERV).
Return value must be checked: 0 on success; non-zero is EAI_* error; EAI_SYSTEM implies errno is set.

functions.name: pr_inet_ntop
functions.signature: const char *pr_inet_ntop(int, const void *, char *, size_t);
functions.description: Wrapper for inet_ntop(3). Converts a network address from binary form (in_addr/in6_addr) to presentation (text) format into the provided buffer.
requirements: af must be AF_INET or AF_INET6.
src must point to a struct in_addr (AF_INET) or struct in6_addr (AF_INET6).
dst must be a valid writable buffer; size must be at least INET_ADDRSTRLEN for AF_INET or INET6_ADDRSTRLEN for AF_INET6.
Returns dst on success; NULL on failure with errno set.

functions.name: pr_inet_pton
functions.description: Wrapper for inet_pton(3). Converts an IPv4/IPv6 presentation (text) address into network (binary) form.
requirements: af must be AF_INET or AF_INET6.
src must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated IPv4/IPv6 literal string (no ports).
dst must point to storage for struct in_addr (AF_INET) or struct in6_addr (AF_INET6).
Return values follow inet_pton: 1 on success, 0 for invalid input text, -1 on error with errno set.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_alloc
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a pr_netaddr_t from the given memory pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid pool pointer from which the allocation is made.
Caller must not free directly; lifetime is tied to the pool.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_dup
functions.description: Duplicates a pr_netaddr_t into memory from the given pool.
requirements: pool must be valid.
Source pr_netaddr_t pointer must be non-NULL and initialized.
Result is pool-managed; do not free directly.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_clear
functions.description: Initializes/clears a pr_netaddr_t to a known state.
requirements: Argument must be a valid, writable pr_netaddr_t pointer.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_addr
functions.description: Resolves a name (IP or DNS) to a primary pr_netaddr_t. If the name has multiple addresses and an array pointer is provided, it is set to an array_header containing additional pr_netaddr_t* results allocated from the pool. On resolution failure, returns NULL and logs an error.
requirements: pool must be valid.
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string containing an IP literal or DNS name.
If extras is non-NULL, it must be a writable pointer to receive an array_header*; the array itself is pool-allocated.
Caller must not modify or free the returned addresses outside pool semantics.
Caller should handle NULL return indicating lookup failure.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_addr2
functions.signature: const pr_netaddr_t *pr_netaddr_get_addr2(pool *, const char *, array_header **, unsigned int);
functions.description: Like pr_netaddr_get_addr() but accepts lookup flags to influence resolution (e.g., include device addresses, exclude DNS, exclude cache).
requirements: pool must be valid.
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
If extras is non-NULL, it must be writable to receive an array_header*.
flags is an OR of PR_NETADDR_GET_ADDR_FL_INCL_DEVICE, PR_NETADDR_GET_ADDR_FL_EXCL_DNS, PR_NETADDR_GET_ADDR_FL_EXCL_CACHE; other bits are unspecified.
Caller should check for NULL return on failure.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_cmp
functions.description: Compares two pr_netaddr_t addresses. Returns -1 with errno=EINVAL if families differ; otherwise compares address bytes (memcmp-like) and returns standard comparison semantics.
requirements: Both pointers must be non-NULL and initialized.
Both addresses must be of the same family (AF_INET or AF_INET6) for a meaningful comparison.
Caller should check for -1 and errno=EINVAL when families differ.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_ncmp
functions.signature: int pr_netaddr_ncmp(const pr_netaddr_t *, const pr_netaddr_t *, unsigned int);
functions.description: Compares the first N bits of two pr_netaddr_t addresses. Returns -1 with errno=EINVAL if families differ; otherwise performs a bitwise-prefix comparison.
requirements: Both pointers must be non-NULL and initialized.
n must be the number of leading bits to compare; must be within the address bit-length for reliable results (inferred).
Both addresses must be same family (AF_INET/AF_INET6).
Check for -1 and errno=EINVAL if families differ.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_fnmatch
functions.signature: int pr_netaddr_fnmatch(const pr_netaddr_t *, const char *, int);
functions.description: Matches a pr_netaddr_t against a glob-style pattern (as for fnmatch). Flags control whether to match DNS and/or IP strings. Returns -1 with errno=EINVAL for NULL args; otherwise TRUE on match, FALSE on no match.
requirements: Address pointer must be non-NULL and initialized.
Pattern must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated glob pattern.
flags is an OR of PR_NETADDR_MATCH_DNS and/or PR_NETADDR_MATCH_IP.
Caller must handle return values: -1/error, 0/false, or non-zero/true.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_sockaddr_len
functions.description: Returns the size of the contained sockaddr (sizeof(struct sockaddr_in) or sizeof(struct sockaddr_in6)). Returns (size_t)-1 with errno=EINVAL for NULL.
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL pr_netaddr_t with a valid family set to AF_INET or AF_INET6.
Caller should check for (size_t)-1 to detect error (per comment).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_inaddr_len
functions.description: Returns the size of the contained in-addr (sizeof(struct in_addr) or sizeof(struct in6_addr)). Returns (size_t)-1 with errno=EINVAL for NULL.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL with a valid AF_INET or AF_INET6 family.
Caller should check for (size_t)-1 indicating error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_family
functions.description: Returns the address family (AF_INET or AF_INET6). Returns -1 with errno=EINVAL if the argument is NULL.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_family
functions.description: Sets the address family on a pr_netaddr_t.
requirements: Argument must be a valid writable pr_netaddr_t pointer.
family must be a supported AF_* constant (AF_INET or AF_INET6).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_inaddr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the contained in_addr (AF_INET) or in6_addr (AF_INET6) within the pr_netaddr_t; returns NULL on error.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and have family set to AF_INET or AF_INET6.
Returned pointer is owned by the pr_netaddr_t; do not free; valid while the object/pool lives.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_sockaddr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the contained sockaddr (sockaddr_in or sockaddr_in6) based on family; returns NULL on error.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and have a valid family set.
Returned pointer is to internal storage; do not free or modify unless explicitly allowed elsewhere.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_sockaddr
functions.description: Sets the contained sockaddr in a pr_netaddr_t from the provided sockaddr. Family must already be set on the pr_netaddr_t.
requirements: pr_netaddr_t pointer must be valid and writable.
Its family must be set prior to calling.
sockaddr pointer must be non-NULL and correspond to the same family (sockaddr_in or sockaddr_in6).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_sockaddr_any
functions.description: Sets the address part of the contained sockaddr to the wildcard (ANY) address for the set family.
requirements: Argument must be a valid writable pr_netaddr_t with family set to AF_INET or AF_INET6.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_port
functions.description: Returns the port number from the contained sockaddr.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and contain a valid sockaddr with port set.
Return is an unsigned integer; byte order not explicitly documented (unknown whether host or network order).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_port
functions.description: Sets the port in the contained sockaddr. The provided port is assumed to already be in network byte order.
requirements: pr_netaddr_t pointer must be valid and writable.
Port value must be provided in network byte order (htons(port)).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (including NULL argument).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_port2
functions.description: Sets the port in the contained sockaddr. The provided port is assumed to be in host byte order.
requirements: pr_netaddr_t pointer must be valid and writable.
Port must be in host byte order; function will convert as needed.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (including NULL argument).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_reverse_dns
functions.description: Enables or disables reverse DNS lookups globally. Returns the previous setting.
requirements: Argument is a boolean-like integer: non-zero to enable, zero to disable (inferred).
Caller should record/handle the returned previous setting if needed.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_dnsstr
functions.description: Returns the DNS name associated with the pr_netaddr_t. If reverse lookups are disabled, returns the IP address string. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returned string points into internal/pool-managed storage; do not free.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_dnsstr_list
functions.description: Returns a list (array_header*) of DNS names for the address. If DNS lookups are disabled, returns an empty list. NULL on error.
requirements: pool must be valid for any allocations.
Address must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returned array is pool-managed; elements are strings managed by the pool; do not free individually.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_ipstr
functions.description: Returns the IP address string associated with the pr_netaddr_t, or NULL on error.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returned pointer is to internal/pool-managed storage; do not free.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_localaddr_str
functions.description: Returns the local host name (from gethostname) duplicated from the given pool, if any.
requirements: pool may be NULL or a valid pool; if non-NULL, returned string is allocated from the pool.
Returned string must not be freed manually; pool manages its lifetime.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_localaddr_str
functions.description: Overrides the local host name used by the server (instead of using gethostname) to avoid DNS lookups for determining the default server address.
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming the local host.
Returns 0/success or -1/error (inferred by convention; exact codes not documented).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_addrno
functions.description: Returns a numeric representation of the address (address number) as a 32-bit value. Specific format is not documented here.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.
Returned numeric format/details are unspecified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_is_loopback
functions.description: Returns TRUE if the address is a loopback address, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.
Return is boolean-like int (non-zero/zero).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_is_rfc1918
functions.description: Returns TRUE if the address is in RFC1918 private ranges; FALSE otherwise. Returns -1 on error with errno set appropriately.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.
Caller must handle -1 indicating error and check errno.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_is_v4
functions.description: Returns TRUE if the given string is an IPv4 address literal, FALSE if not, and -1 on error (errno set).
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle -1 indicating error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_is_v6
functions.description: Returns TRUE if the given string is an IPv6 address literal, FALSE if not, and -1 on error (errno set).
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Caller must handle -1 indicating error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_is_v4mappedv6
functions.description: Returns TRUE if the address is AF_INET6 and contains an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address; FALSE otherwise. Returns -1 on error.
requirements: Argument must be non-NULL and initialized.
Caller must handle -1 indicating error.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_v6tov4
functions.description: Converts an IPv4-mapped IPv6 netaddr to a pure IPv4 pr_netaddr_t allocated from the given pool. Returns NULL if input is not IPv4-mapped IPv6.
requirements: pool must be valid.
addr must be non-NULL and initialized to an AF_INET6 IPv4-mapped address for conversion to succeed.
Returned object is pool-managed.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_v4tov6
functions.description: Converts an IPv4 pr_netaddr_t to an IPv4-mapped IPv6 pr_netaddr_t allocated from the given pool. Returns NULL if input is not IPv4.
requirements: pool must be valid.
addr must be non-NULL and initialized to an AF_INET address for conversion to succeed.
Returned object is pool-managed.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_use_ipv6
functions.description: Returns TRUE if IPv6 support is enabled at runtime, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: No arguments. Caller should treat non-zero as enabled.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_disable_ipv6
functions.description: Disables runtime use of IPv6 functionality (if supported).
requirements: Affects global/runtime state; should be called before operations that depend on IPv6 state (inferred).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_enable_ipv6
functions.description: Enables runtime use of IPv6 functionality (if supported).
requirements: Affects global/runtime state; should be called before operations that depend on IPv6 state (inferred).

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_sess_local_addr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to static memory containing the session's local netaddr. Do not modify the memory. Returns NULL if no session info exists.
requirements: Caller must not modify or free the returned pointer.
Pointer may be NULL; caller must check before use.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_sess_remote_addr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to static memory containing the session's remote netaddr. Do not modify the memory. Returns NULL if no session info exists.
requirements: Caller must not modify or free the returned pointer.
Pointer may be NULL; caller must check before use.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_get_sess_remote_name
functions.description: Returns the session's remote name string (from static/session memory). Do not modify. May be NULL if not available.
requirements: Caller must not modify or free the returned pointer.
Pointer may be NULL; check before use.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_set_sess_addrs
functions.description: Initializes/updates static memory that holds the session local/remote netaddr information.
requirements: Should be called when session addressing becomes available; exact timing not detailed in header (unknown).
No arguments; affects global/session state.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_clear_cache
functions.description: Clears the cache of all netaddr objects.
requirements: Global/stateful effect; safe to call to drop cached address/DNS data.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_clear_dnscache
functions.description: Clears cached DNS names for a given IP address string.
requirements: ip_addr must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated IP address string.
Only affects cache entries related to the provided address.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_clear_ipcache
functions.description: Clears cached IP addresses for a given DNS name.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated DNS name string.
Only affects cache entries related to the provided name.

functions.name: pr_netaddr_validate_dns_str
functions.description: Validates the provided DNS name string and returns a (possibly modified) string. Intended for ensuring returned DNS names are acceptable.
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL mutable C string buffer.
Returned pointer refers to the (same) buffer; do not free separately.

functions.name: init_netaddr
functions.description: Initializes internal netaddr subsystem state. Marked for internal use only.
requirements: Should be called once during initialization by internal code; not intended for external callers.
No arguments; sets up internal state.

functions.name: pr_netio_buffer_alloc
functions.description: Allocate and attach (or return) a buffer object for the given NetIO stream. Typically used before reads/writes that rely on an internal stream buffer.
requirements: nstrm must be a valid, initialized pr_netio_stream_t pointer.
Returns NULL on allocation failure (caller must handle).
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pr_buffer_t is tied to the stream; do not free it manually unless the implementation explicitly allows it (unknown).

functions.name: pr_netio_abort
functions.description: Request that I/O on the given stream be aborted as soon as possible. Sets internal abort state so subsequent I/O returns promptly (e.g., as -2 when PR_NETIO_SESS_INTR is set).
requirements: Argument must be a valid, open pr_netio_stream_t.
After calling, next poll/read/write may return early per the session flags (caller must handle early returns).

functions.name: pr_netio_lingering_abort
functions.description: Abort I/O on the given stream, performing a lingering-style abort per flags. Allows controlling whether underlying socket shutdown occurs during abort.
requirements: First argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t.
Second argument is a flags bitmask; NETIO_LINGERING_CLOSE_FL_NO_SHUTDOWN disables shutdown during abort.
Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error (caller must check).
Exact linger semantics and additional flags beyond NETIO_LINGERING_CLOSE_FL_NO_SHUTDOWN are unknown.

functions.name: pr_netio_close
functions.description: Close the given NetIO stream using the active NetIO provider. Frees/cleans stream resources and closes its file descriptor.
requirements: Argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t representing an open stream.
Returns 0 on success, or -1 on error; PR_NETIO_ERRNO(s) may hold details (caller must check and handle).
After success, the stream should not be used again (unless reopened via pr_netio_reopen).

functions.name: pr_netio_lingering_close
functions.description: Close a stream using lingering semantics controlled by flags (e.g., optionally avoiding shutdown). Useful for ensuring pending data is handled or for avoiding blocking closes.
requirements: First argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t.
Second argument is a flags bitmask; supports NETIO_LINGERING_CLOSE_FL_NO_SHUTDOWN.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (caller must check).
Exact linger timing/behavior details are unknown from this header.

functions.name: pr_netio_gets
functions.description: Read a text line from the stream into buf, similar to fgets(), stopping at newline or buffer limit. Returns buf on success or NULL on EOF/error.
requirements: buf must be a valid writable buffer of size at least buflen.
buflen must be > 0 to store any data including terminator if applicable.
The stream must be valid and readable.
Caller must check for NULL return to detect EOF/error; error details may be in PR_NETIO_ERRNO(stream).

functions.name: pr_netio_open
functions.signature: pr_netio_stream_t *pr_netio_open(pool *p, int strm_type, int fd, int mode);
functions.description: Create and open a NetIO stream for a given file descriptor, stream type, and I/O mode using memory from p. Stream type selects which registered NetIO provider is used (control, data, or other).
requirements: p must be a valid memory pool.
strm_type should be one of PR_NETIO_STRM_CTRL, PR_NETIO_STRM_DATA, or PR_NETIO_STRM_OTHR (bitmask as required by implementation).
fd should be a valid file descriptor appropriate for network I/O.
mode should be PR_NETIO_IO_RD or PR_NETIO_IO_WR (patterned after open(2)).
Returns NULL on failure (caller must handle).

functions.name: pr_netio_postopen
functions.description: Run provider-specific post-open handling on a stream (e.g., setting options) after pr_netio_open or reopen. Ensures stream is ready for I/O.
requirements: Argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t that has been opened.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_netio_printf
functions.description: Formatted write to the stream, like fprintf() to a network stream. Blocks/polls per NetIO policy before writing.
requirements: Stream must be valid and writable.
fmt must be a non-NULL format string; following arguments must match fmt.
Returns number of bytes written (>=0) on success, or -1 on error (caller must check).
May internally call pr_netio_poll(); interruptions may occur per PR_NETIO_SESS_INTR.

functions.name: pr_netio_vprintf
functions.signature: int pr_netio_vprintf(pr_netio_stream_t *, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of pr_netio_printf() for formatted writes using an existing va_list.
requirements: Stream must be valid and writable.
fmt must be non-NULL; ap must be a valid, initialized va_list.
Returns number of bytes written (>=0) on success, or -1 on error (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_netio_printf_async
functions.description: Formatted write intended for use in async contexts (e.g., inside alarm/signal handlers). Avoids blocking poll calls that could hang if send queues are full and the socket is closed.
requirements: Only use in contexts where blocking is not allowed (e.g., signal/alarm handlers).
Stream must be valid and writable.
fmt must be a non-NULL format string; subsequent arguments must match fmt.
Returns number of bytes written (>=0) on success, or -1 on error (caller must check).
Because it is async-safe oriented, available operations may be limited; do not assume full printf semantics beyond what implementation guarantees (details unknown).

functions.name: pr_netio_poll
functions.description: Poll the stream for readiness, mitigating race conditions around signal delivery vs. read/write. Uses a configurable timeout and session flags to decide whether to restart or return early.
requirements: Argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t.
On timeout with PR_NETIO_SESS_ABORT set or PR_NETIO_SESS_INTR with errno==EINTR, returns 1; returns 0 when data is available; returns -1 on other errors (caller must handle all cases).
Poll interval is set via pr_netio_set_poll_interval(); default/reset via pr_netio_reset_poll_interval().

functions.name: pr_netio_read
functions.signature: int pr_netio_read(pr_netio_stream_t *, char *buf, size_t nbytes, int min_bytes);
functions.description: Read up to nbytes from the stream into buf. The call returns once at least min_bytes have been read, then returns 1 (or greater).
requirements: Stream must be valid and readable.
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least nbytes bytes.
min_bytes specifies the minimum number of bytes that must be read before returning; it should be >= 0 and not exceed nbytes (inferred).
Return value semantics beyond “1 (or greater) when min_bytes satisfied” are not fully documented; caller must check for negative values as errors (inferred).

functions.name: pr_netio_reopen
functions.description: Reopen an existing NetIO stream on a new or existing file descriptor, possibly changing its I/O mode.
requirements: First argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t (typically previously opened).
fd should be a valid file descriptor.
mode should be PR_NETIO_IO_RD or PR_NETIO_IO_WR.
Returns NULL on failure (caller must handle).

functions.name: pr_netio_shutdown
functions.description: Shutdown part or all of a full-duplex stream, analogous to shutdown(2). The how parameter selects read, write, or both directions.
requirements: Stream must be valid.
how must be a valid shutdown mode (e.g., SHUT_RD, SHUT_WR, or SHUT_RDWR; exact constants depend on platform).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_netio_telnet_gets
functions.description: Read a line from a stream like pr_netio_gets(), but processes special Telnet IAC sequences (e.g., handling the ABOR command and quirks of some clients). ctrl_strm may be used for ABOR handling.
requirements: buf must be a valid writable buffer of at least buflen bytes.
buflen must be > 0.
data_strm must be valid and readable.
ctrl_strm must be a valid stream when Telnet control handling is required; may be NULL if not applicable (unknown).
Returns buf on success, or NULL on EOF/error (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_netio_telnet_gets2
functions.signature: int pr_netio_telnet_gets2(char *buf, size_t buflen, pr_netio_stream_t *data_strm, pr_netio_stream_t *ctrl_strm);
functions.description: Like pr_netio_telnet_gets(), but returns the number of bytes stored in buf, or -1 on error. Telnet IAC/ABOR handling is applied.
requirements: buf must be a valid writable buffer of at least buflen bytes.
buflen must be > 0.
data_strm must be valid and readable.
ctrl_strm must be valid when Telnet control handling is needed (unknown if NULL allowed).
Caller must handle -1 on error and 0..buflen on success.

functions.name: pr_netio_write
functions.description: Write up to nbytes from buf to the stream, blocking/polling per NetIO policy.
requirements: Stream must be valid and writable.
buf must point to at least nbytes bytes of readable data.
Returns number of bytes written (>=0) on success, or -1 on error (caller must check).
May internally use pr_netio_poll(); interruptions may occur per PR_NETIO_SESS_INTR.

functions.name: pr_netio_write_async
functions.description: Write data to the stream in a nonblocking manner. Temporarily sets the underlying fd to O_NONBLOCK to avoid kernel-level blocking, saving and restoring original flags.
requirements: Stream must be valid and writable.
buf must point to at least nbytes bytes of readable data.
Intended for contexts where blocking must be avoided; caller must be prepared for partial writes or EWOULDBLOCK-like behavior (inferred).
Returns number of bytes written (>=0) on success, or -1 on error (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_netio_reset_poll_interval
functions.description: Reset the stream's poll interval to the default value used by the NetIO layer.
requirements: Argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t.

functions.name: pr_netio_set_poll_interval
functions.description: Set the stream's poll interval (used by pr_netio_poll and I/O wait logic) to the specified value.
requirements: Argument must be a valid pr_netio_stream_t.
interval_ms is a timeout in milliseconds (unit inferred from naming); must be a non-negative unsigned value.

functions.name: pr_alloc_netio
functions.description: Allocate a NetIO provider object from pool p and initialize all callbacks to default handlers.
requirements: p must be a valid memory pool.
Returns NULL on allocation failure (caller must check).
Callbacks are set to defaults; caller may override before registration.

functions.name: pr_alloc_netio2
functions.description: Allocate a NetIO provider object with default callbacks, recording the owning module and owner name for identification/registration.
requirements: p must be a valid memory pool.
owner may be NULL or a valid module pointer (exact requirement unknown).
owner_name may be NULL or a constant string (exact requirement unknown).
Returns NULL on allocation failure (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_register_netio
functions.description: Register the given NetIO provider for the specified stream types. If netio is NULL, instantiate and register the default NetIO.
requirements: strm_types is a bitmask of PR_NETIO_STRM_CTRL, PR_NETIO_STRM_DATA, and/or PR_NETIO_STRM_OTHR.
If netio is non-NULL, it must be allocated/initialized (e.g., via pr_alloc_netio/pr_alloc_netio2) with valid callbacks.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_unregister_netio
functions.description: Unregister any NetIO providers associated with the specified stream type mask.
requirements: strm_types is a bitmask of PR_NETIO_STRM_CTRL, PR_NETIO_STRM_DATA, and/or PR_NETIO_STRM_OTHR.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (caller must check).

functions.name: pr_get_netio
functions.description: Return the currently registered NetIO provider for the given stream type without modifying registration.
requirements: strm_type should be one of PR_NETIO_STRM_CTRL, PR_NETIO_STRM_DATA, or PR_NETIO_STRM_OTHR.
Returns NULL if none is registered (caller must handle).

functions.name: init_netio
functions.description: Initialize the NetIO subsystem and its defaults. Should be called during server startup before using NetIO functions.
requirements: Must be called once during initialization before creating/using NetIO streams (inferred).

functions.name: Blowfish_encipher
functions.description: Encrypts a single 64-bit Blowfish block in place using the provided Blowfish context. The block is passed as two consecutive 32-bit words. Typical usage: initialize and key the context (e.g., via blf_key or the expand-state functions), then call to encrypt each block.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null and must have been initialized and keyed (e.g., via Blowfish_initstate followed by a key expansion function or via blf_key) before use.
The u_int32_t* must point to at least two consecutive 32-bit words representing one 64-bit block; data is modified in place.
Callers must not concurrently modify the same blf_ctx while calling this function.
Alignment suitable for u_int32_t access is required for the data pointer.

functions.name: Blowfish_decipher
functions.description: Decrypts a single 64-bit Blowfish block in place using the provided Blowfish context. The block is passed as two consecutive 32-bit words. Typical usage: after context initialization and key setup, call to decrypt each block.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null and must have been initialized and keyed prior to use.
The u_int32_t* must point to at least two consecutive 32-bit words representing one 64-bit block; data is modified in place.
Callers must not concurrently modify the same blf_ctx while calling this function.
Alignment suitable for u_int32_t access is required for the data pointer.

functions.name: Blowfish_initstate
functions.description: Initializes a Blowfish context to the algorithm’s initial P-array and S-box constants, preparing it for subsequent key expansion. Typical usage: call once on a fresh context before any expand-state operations or use a higher-level helper like blf_key which performs both steps.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null.
Must be called before Blowfish_expand0state/Blowfish_expandstate if those are used directly.

functions.name: Blowfish_expand0state
functions.description: Expands an initialized Blowfish context with a key only (no additional data/salt), completing the Blowfish key schedule. Note: Comments indicate keys up to 56 bytes are standard; up to 72 bytes may be utilized by this implementation. Usage: call after Blowfish_initstate when performing custom state setup; blf_key wraps this sequence for standard Blowfish.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null and must have been initialized via Blowfish_initstate before calling.
If key length (u_int16_t) is greater than 0, the const u_int8_t* key pointer must be non-null.
Key length should not exceed BLF_MAXUTILIZED ((BLF_N+2)*4 == 72 bytes) per the comment; standard Blowfish keys are up to BLF_MAXKEYLEN (56 bytes).
Caller should ensure the provided key material is valid and accessible for the specified length.

functions.name: Blowfish_expandstate
functions.signature: void Blowfish_expandstate(blf_ctx *, const u_int8_t *, u_int16_t, const u_int8_t *, u_int16_t);
functions.description: Expands an initialized Blowfish context with both key material and additional data (often used as salt) to produce a customized key schedule. Typical usage in constructions like bcrypt: call after Blowfish_initstate, optionally interleaving with additional expansions.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null and must have been initialized via Blowfish_initstate before calling.
If key length is greater than 0, the key pointer must be non-null.
If data length is greater than 0, the data pointer must be non-null.
Key length should not exceed BLF_MAXUTILIZED (72 bytes) per the comment; standard Blowfish keys are up to BLF_MAXKEYLEN (56 bytes).
Caller must ensure both key and data buffers are valid for the specified lengths during the call.

functions.name: blf_key
functions.description: Standard Blowfish key setup helper. Initializes and expands the context with the provided key, effectively performing Blowfish_initstate followed by Blowfish_expand0state. Use this to prepare a context for blf_enc/blf_dec.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null.
If key length is greater than 0, the key pointer must be non-null.
Key length should be within Blowfish’s limits; standard keys are up to BLF_MAXKEYLEN (56 bytes), though up to BLF_MAXUTILIZED (72 bytes) may be utilized by the implementation per comment.
Must be called (or an equivalent initialization/expansion sequence performed) before calling blf_enc or blf_dec.

functions.name: blf_enc
functions.description: Encrypts multiple 64-bit blocks in place using the provided Blowfish context. The data buffer is an array of 32-bit words; the third parameter specifies the number of 64-bit blocks to process.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null and must have been initialized and keyed (e.g., via blf_key).
The u_int32_t* data must point to an array containing at least 2 * n 32-bit words where n is the u_int16_t block count; data is modified in place.
Alignment suitable for u_int32_t access is required for the data pointer.
Callers must not concurrently modify the same blf_ctx while this function operates.

functions.name: blf_dec
functions.description: Decrypts multiple 64-bit blocks in place using the provided Blowfish context. The data buffer is an array of 32-bit words; the third parameter specifies the number of 64-bit blocks to process.
requirements: The blf_ctx pointer must be non-null and must have been initialized and keyed (e.g., via blf_key).
The u_int32_t* data must point to an array containing at least 2 * n 32-bit words where n is the u_int16_t block count; data is modified in place.
Alignment suitable for u_int32_t access is required for the data pointer.
Callers must not concurrently modify the same blf_ctx while this function operates.

functions.name: Blowfish_stream2word
functions.description: Converts a byte stream into a 32-bit word, typically by consuming bytes from the stream and updating a position/index pointer (commonly used during key expansion). Exact assembly (endianness, cycling behavior) is not documented here; inferred from naming and typical Blowfish implementations.
requirements: If the length parameter is greater than 0, the const u_int8_t* stream pointer must be non-null and reference at least that many bytes.
The u_int16_t* position/index pointer must be non-null and points to a caller-maintained index that may be updated by the function.
Behavior for a length of 0 is unspecified; callers should avoid passing 0 unless they know the implementation’s behavior.
Caller must handle the returned 32-bit value appropriately; no side-channel error reporting is indicated.

functions.name: bcrypt_hashpass
functions.signature: int bcrypt_hashpass(const char *, const char *, char *, size_t);
functions.description: Computes a bcrypt password hash. Takes a password string, a salt string, and writes the resulting hash string into the provided buffer. Return value is an int status; exact success/error conventions are not specified in this header. Typical usage: provide a valid bcrypt salt and a buffer large enough to hold the resulting hash string.
requirements: Password and salt pointers must be non-null and point to NUL-terminated strings.
The salt must be a format accepted by the implementation (commonly a bcrypt salt string). If invalid, the function is expected to fail.
The output buffer pointer must be non-null and point to writable memory of at least hashlen bytes; the function writes the hash string there and may NUL-terminate it.

The hashlen value must accurately reflect the size of the output buffer; it must be large enough to hold the full bcrypt hash string produced by this implementation (exact minimum size is not specified here).
Caller must check the int return value to detect failure; exact return codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: pr_parser_prepare
functions.description: Initializes the configuration parser, allocating any necessary internal resources from the given memory pool. Optionally returns, via parsed_servers, the list head of configured server_rec structures after parsing completes. Typical usage: call once before parsing any configuration, then call pr_parser_cleanup() afterward.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized pool pointer able to outlive all parser allocations until pr_parser_cleanup() is called.
parsed_servers may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to storage for an xaset_t* and will be assigned after parsing completes.
Must be paired with a subsequent pr_parser_cleanup() to release internal parser state.
Should be called before any parse operations (e.g., pr_parser_parse_file, context push/open/close).

functions.name: pr_parser_cleanup
functions.description: Clears and frees any internal parser state previously initialized by pr_parser_prepare() and/or created during parsing. Call after parsing is finished.
requirements: Must be called after parsing is done to clear internal state.
Should only be called after a successful pr_parser_prepare(); calling without prior prepare may be undefined.
Must not be called concurrently with other parser operations.

functions.name: pr_parser_config_ctxt_open
functions.description: Pushes a start-of-configuration-context marker onto the parser stack. The name identifies the config block (e.g., "Directory", "Anonymous"). Returns the new/opened config_rec for that context.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming the context.
Must be balanced with a corresponding pr_parser_config_ctxt_close() eventually.
Parser must be prepared (pr_parser_prepare called) before use.

functions.name: pr_parser_config_ctxt_close

A successful compile must occur before calling pr_regexp_exec on this handle.

functions.name: pr_regexp_compile

functions.description: Compiles the pattern into the pr_regex_t using PCRE if enabled, otherwise POSIX regex. Returns an integer status; use pr_regexp_error to translate any error code into a human-readable string. Engine selection can also be influenced globally via pr_regexp_set_engine.
requirements: pre must be a valid, allocated pr_regex_t (from pr_regexp_alloc).
pattern must be a valid, NUL-terminated string; NULL is not allowed.

Call this successfully before pr_regexp_exec on the same handle.

functions.description: Formats a human-readable error message for a regex operation result code (from compile/exec) into the provided buffer. May use engine-specific error reporting, using the pre context. Returns a size value for the generated/attempted message; exact return semantics (bytes written vs. required size) are not specified here.
requirements: buf must point to writable memory of at least bufsz bytes; bufsz should be greater than 0.

If bufsz is too small, the message may be truncated; exact truncation behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: pr_regexp_get_pattern

functions.name: pr_regexp_exec

functions.description: Executes the compiled regular expression against the provided input string. Optionally captures up to nmatches match groups into matches. The flags are engine-specific (POSIX or PCRE). Match limits cap engine work; they are honored only when PCRE support is enabled. Returns an integer status; use pr_regexp_error to translate errors.
requirements: pre must be a valid pr_regex_t that has been successfully compiled.
str must be a valid, NUL-terminated input string; NULL is not allowed.
If nmatches > 0, matches must point to an array of at least nmatches regmatch_t elements; if nmatches == 0, matches may be NULL.
flags must be appropriate for the underlying engine; invalid flags may cause failure.
match_limit and match_limit_recursion define engine work limits; these are only properly honored when PCRE support is enabled; valid ranges are not documented.
Callers should check the return code and use pr_regexp_error for diagnostics.

functions.name: pr_regexp_set_limits
functions.signature: int pr_regexp_set_limits(unsigned long match_limit, unsigned long match_limit_recursion);
functions.description: Sets default matching limits (overall work and recursive/stack depth) to be applied when explicit limits are not provided by callers. Intended for daemon/vhost-wide configuration. These limits are only properly honored when PCRE support is enabled. Returns an integer status (exact semantics unspecified).
requirements: Should be called during initialization/configuration before regex operations that rely on defaults; exact timing not strictly specified.
match_limit and match_limit_recursion should be non-pathological values; the valid ranges are not documented here.
Effects apply only when PCRE is enabled; with pure POSIX engines, limits may be ignored.

functions.name: pr_regexp_set_engine
functions.description: Sets the regex engine to use globally (e.g., "POSIX" or "PCRE"). The value is case-insensitive. Useful for forcing POSIX semantics even when PCRE is available. Returns an integer status; exact values unspecified.
requirements: engine must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a supported engine (e.g., "POSIX" or "PCRE").

functions.name: pr_response_add

A response pool/list must be initialized; exact error-specific handling is unknown (not documented in this header).

functions.name: pr_response_block

block should be treated as a boolean flag (non-zero to block, zero to unblock) inferred from the name/signature.

functions.name: pr_response_clear

functions.name: pr_response_flush

If *list is non-NULL, it must reference a response list created by this subsystem.
Caller should not use previously queued response nodes after flushing, as the list will be cleared.

functions.name: pr_response_get_last

resp_code must be a non-NULL pointer to a const char* receiver; on success, *resp_code will be set to the code string.
response_msg must be a non-NULL pointer to a const char* receiver; on success, *response_msg will be set to the message string.
Caller is responsible for the lifetime of pool p; the returned strings remain valid while p is alive.
Exact return codes are unknown; caller should check for non-zero/zero per project conventions (not specified here).

functions.name: pr_response_send
functions.description: Formats and sends a response (code and message) immediately to the client. Uses printf-style formatting for the message.
requirements: code must be a valid, null-terminated C string representing the response code.
fmt must be a valid, null-terminated C format string (printf-style).
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt (printf-style).
Should not be called while responses are blocked if immediate sending is required (blocking behavior is controlled by pr_response_block).

functions.name: pr_response_send_async
functions.description: Formats and sends a response asynchronously. Uses printf-style formatting. Exact scheduling/queueing semantics are not documented here.

fmt must be a valid, null-terminated C format string (printf-style).
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt (printf-style).
Asynchronous behavior specifics (threading/timing) are unknown from this header; callers must not assume immediate delivery.

functions.name: pr_response_send_raw

requirements: fmt must be a valid, null-terminated C format string (printf-style).
The variable arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt (printf-style).
Caller should ensure the formatted line is suitable for direct transmission (e.g., includes any required protocol code/prefix).

functions.name: pr_response_register_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback that can handle/adjust a response line before it is sent to the client. If no callback is registered, lines are sent as-is. The handler receives a pool and a printf-style format with arguments and must return a C string to be sent.
requirements: handler must be a valid function pointer taking (pool*, const char*, ...) and returning char*.
The handler should be able to use the provided pool p for any needed allocations; the returned string must remain valid at least until the send operation completes (exact lifetime not documented).
The handler must interpret fmt and its varargs in a printf-compatible manner.
Only one handler is implied; subsequent calls replace the previous handler (inferred from typical register semantics; exact behavior not documented).

functions.name: pr_response_get_pool
functions.description: Returns the memory pool currently used for response lists and allocations related to responses.
requirements: Must be called after the response subsystem is initialized; otherwise the returned pointer may be NULL or invalid (not specified in header).
Caller must not free or destroy the returned pool unless it owns the lifetime management per the broader system’s conventions.

functions.name: pr_response_set_pool
functions.description: Sets the memory pool to be used for response lists and related allocations.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized pool object compatible with the system’s pool allocator.
The pool must outlive any responses allocated from it; destroying p prematurely will invalidate response data.
Should be called before adding/sending responses that rely on pool-based allocation.

functions.name: pr_get_scoreboard

Callers should check the return value and handle failure appropriately; specific error codes are not documented here.

functions.name: pr_set_scoreboard_mutex
functions.description: Sets the filesystem path to the scoreboard mutex/lock file. Use before opening/creating the scoreboard so locking uses this path.

Callers should check the return value for success/failure; error codes are not specified here.

functions.description: Closes the scoreboard, optionally keeping the mutex/lock state. The keep_mutex flag likely controls whether the mutex file or lock remains after close (details not documented here).
requirements: The keep_mutex parameter is treated as a boolean flag; exact accepted range/values are not documented.
Should be called after you are done reading/updating the scoreboard to release resources.
Callers should check the return value and handle errors; specific error codes are not specified here.

functions.name: pr_delete_scoreboard
functions.description: Deletes/removes the scoreboard (and possibly its lock/mutex). Intended for cleanup when the scoreboard is no longer needed.
requirements: Call only when no other process/thread needs the scoreboard to avoid races or orphaned readers (not enforced by this header).
No return value; any error reporting mechanism is not specified here.

functions.name: pr_open_scoreboard
functions.description: Opens (and possibly creates) the scoreboard for subsequent read/write operations. The integer parameter likely controls open mode/flags (not documented here).
requirements: The integer parameter must be valid for the expected open/mode semantics; exact meaning is unknown from this header.
Callers should check the return value and handle failure; specific error codes are not specified here.

functions.name: pr_restore_scoreboard
functions.description: Restores/validates the scoreboard state from persistent storage, including checking header magic/version as needed. Intended to be called during startup or recovery.

Callers should check the return value; negative values may indicate compatibility problems (e.g., magic/version), but exact codes are not specified here.

Callers should check the return value and handle failure; specific error codes are not specified here.

functions.name: pr_scoreboard_get_daemon_pid

functions.name: pr_scoreboard_entry_del

The int signal parameter should be a valid signal number for the platform (e.g., SIGTERM, SIGHUP).

Callers should check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: pr_scoreboard_entry_lock
functions.description: Locks or unlocks a specific scoreboard entry or performs per-entry synchronization. The exact meaning of the two integer parameters (e.g., entry identifier and lock mode) is not documented here.

Callers should check the return value and handle failure.

functions.name: pr_session_get_disconnect_reason

functions.description: Returns the current protocol name in use for this session (for example, a string like "FTP" or "SSH2"). Pass flags to influence formatting/selection; use PR_SESS_PROTO_FL_LOGOUT when retrieving the name for login/logout messages.

The returned const char* is read-only; do not modify or free it.
Call from a valid session context; behavior outside a session is unspecified.
If the protocol has not been set/initialized, the return value may be NULL or implementation-defined (not documented).

Call from a valid session context; behavior outside a session is unspecified.
