Return value semantics are not specified here; check for nonzero/negative as implementation defines.

functions.name: pr_session_set_protocol
functions.description: Sets the current protocol name for this session (e.g., "FTP", "SSH2"). Affects what pr_session_get_protocol returns, including for login/logout messages.
requirements: The const char* argument should be a valid, NUL-terminated protocol name string; do not pass NULL.
Only call in a valid session context before or during login where protocol changes are meaningful; later changes may affect logging (not documented).
Returns an int status code; exact success/error values are not documented here.

functions.name: xaset_create
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new xaset (an intrusive, doubly-linked set/list) from the given memory pool. If a compare callback is supplied, the set can support sorted operations; otherwise it behaves as an unsorted container. Typical usage: create once per container, then insert/remove xasetmember_t nodes that are embedded in user structs.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized ProFTPD memory pool; it must outlive the returned xaset_t.
compare may be NULL if only unsorted operations (e.g., xaset_insert, xaset_insert_end, xaset_remove) are used; a non-NULL comparator is required for sorted insertion (xaset_insert_sort).
The caller owns the returned xaset_t within the lifetime of p; the set is allocated from p and freed when p is destroyed.
This function must be called before using the returned xaset_t in any insert/remove operations.

functions.name: xaset_copy
functions.signature: xaset_t *xaset_copy(pool *p, xaset_t *src, size_t param, XASET_MCOPY mcopy)
functions.description: Creates a new xaset in pool p that is a copy of the src set. Copying of individual members is controlled by the mcopy callback; if provided, it should duplicate a given xasetmember_t node for insertion into the new set. The exact semantics of the size_t parameter are not documented in this header and are unknown (could influence copy behavior).
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized memory pool that will outlive the returned set.
src must be a valid, initialized xaset_t.

mcopy, if non-NULL, must return a newly allocated or otherwise valid xasetmember_t suitable for insertion into the destination set; ownership/lifetime must be compatible with pool p. If NULL, copy semantics are unknown from this header.
The meaning and valid range of param are unknown from this header; callers must consult implementation/docs to supply a correct value.
The returned set is allocated from p; it will be freed with p.

functions.name: xaset_insert
functions.description: Inserts the given member node at the head (or default position) of the set. Intended for use with intrusive nodes (xasetmember_t) embedded in user-defined structs.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized xaset_t.
m must be a valid xasetmember_t that is not currently linked into any set (its next/prev should not point into another list).
The lifetime of the object containing m must extend at least until the member is removed from the set.
Return value is an int status; exact success/failure convention is not documented here (nonzero vs zero unknown). Callers should check and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: xaset_insert_end
functions.description: Appends the given member node to the end (tail) of the set. Useful for preserving insertion order in an unsorted set.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized xaset_t.
m must be a valid xasetmember_t not currently linked into any set.
The lifetime of the object containing m must extend at least until the member is removed from the set.
Return value is an int status; exact success/failure convention is not documented here and must be checked by the caller.

functions.name: xaset_insert_sort
functions.description: Inserts the given member into the set according to the set's comparator, maintaining sorted order. The integer parameter controls behavior, but its specific meaning/flags are not documented in this header and are unknown.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized xaset_t created with a non-NULL comparator; otherwise sorted insertion cannot be performed.
m must be a valid xasetmember_t not currently linked into any set.
flags must be chosen according to the library’s documented semantics; their meaning is unknown from this header.
The comparator provided at xaset_create must be able to compare the specific member type used; it will be invoked with xasetmember_t pointers corresponding to embedded nodes.
Return value is an int status; exact success/failure convention is not documented here and must be checked by the caller.

functions.name: xaset_remove
functions.description: Removes the specified member from the set’s linkage. After removal, the member is no longer part of the set; ownership of the member remains with the caller.
requirements: set must be a valid, initialized xaset_t.
m must be a member that is currently linked into set; removing a member not in the set may fail or have undefined behavior (unspecified here).
After removal, m should not be used as if part of any set until reinserted.
Return value is an int status; exact success/failure convention is not documented here and must be checked by the caller.

functions.name: pr_signals_block
functions.description: Blocks delivery/handling of process signals within ProFTPD. Intended to be called around critical sections where asynchronous signal handling could interfere. The function has no parameters and no return value.
requirements: Should be paired with a subsequent call to pr_signals_unblock() to restore normal signal handling (pairing inferred from common naming pattern; exact nesting/paired semantics unknown).
Call only in contexts where temporarily deferring signal processing is safe for the caller’s logic.
Thread-safety/recursion semantics are unknown.

functions.name: pr_signals_unblock
functions.description: Unblocks delivery/handling of process signals previously blocked via pr_signals_block(). Restores normal signal processing.
requirements: Should typically be called after a matching pr_signals_block() to resume normal signal handling (exact nesting/paired semantics unknown).
Call only when the caller is ready for pending signals to be handled.
Thread-safety/recursion semantics are unknown.

functions.name: pr_signals_handle
functions.description: Processes any pending signal interruptions, intentionally adding a small delay to avoid tight spin loops and excessive CPU usage. This is the standard signal-processing entry point to be used in most situations.
requirements: Intended for general use when handling pending signals; no parameters and no return value.
May introduce a small delay by design; call sites must tolerate this latency.
Must not be used when a delay is unacceptable; use pr_signals_handle_without_delay() instead in those specific cases.

functions.name: pr_signals_handle_without_delay
functions.description: Processes pending signal interruptions without the small delay normally used to prevent tight loops. Per the header comment, only use this variant in very specific situations (e.g., daemon process context and connection acceptance) where added delay is undesirable.
requirements: Use only in specific situations where no delay should be added, such as in the daemon process or during connection acceptance, per the header comments.
Callers must ensure that running without the protective delay will not cause busy-waiting or CPU spikes in their call path.
No parameters and no return value.

functions.name: pr_signals_handle_disconnect
functions.description: Signal handler routine for handling a disconnect-related signal (exact signal(s) not documented in this header). Designed to be installed as a signal handler; receives the signal number as its int parameter and returns RETSIGTYPE (platform-dependent signal handler return type).
requirements: Must be invoked by the system as a signal handler or called with a valid POSIX signal number; the int parameter is the signal number.
Only perform operations that are safe in an async-signal context when this runs (typical signal handler constraint; specific actions performed are unknown).
Exact signals it handles and side effects are unknown; refer to implementation for details.

functions.name: pr_signals_handle_event
functions.description: Generic signal handler routine for processing a signal-driven event (exact semantics not documented in this header). Intended to be registered as a signal handler; takes the signal number as its int parameter and returns RETSIGTYPE.
requirements: Must be installed/used as a signal handler or called with a valid signal number; the int parameter is the signal number provided by the OS.
Only async-signal-safe operations should be assumed permissible while this handler runs (specific behavior unknown).
Exact signals and effects are unknown; consult implementation.

functions.name: pr_stash_add_symbol
functions.description: Registers/adds a symbol into ProFTPD's internal symbol table (“stash”) under the specified stash type (e.g., configuration, command, auth, hook). Intended to be used by modules to publish their symbols for later lookup/removal. Return value semantics are not documented here; success/failure details are unknown.
requirements: stash_type must be a valid pr_stash_type_t value (PR_SYM_CONF, PR_SYM_CMD, PR_SYM_AUTH, or PR_SYM_HOOK).

requirements: stash_type must be a valid pr_stash_type_t value.
name must be a non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated string naming the symbol.
prev_sym may be NULL to start a new lookup/iteration; otherwise it should be a symbol pointer previously returned by this function for the same stash_type and name.
The int* parameter, if non-NULL, must point to writable memory; its purpose and value range are unknown. It may be NULL if not needed (inferred).
Returned pointer type/layout depends on stash_type and is unspecified here; callers must cast appropriately and must not assume ownership or mutability unless documented elsewhere.

functions.description: Variant of pr_stash_get_symbol that additionally provides an unsigned int* output/auxiliary parameter (purpose unknown), likely returning extra attributes/flags. Supports iterative lookup via prev_sym. Returns a pointer to a matching symbol or NULL if no (more) matches are found or on error (semantics not documented).
requirements: stash_type must be a valid pr_stash_type_t value.
name must be a non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated string naming the symbol.
prev_sym may be NULL to start a new lookup/iteration; otherwise it should be a symbol pointer previously returned by this function for the same stash_type and name.
The int* parameter, if provided, must point to writable memory; meaning is unknown. It may be NULL if not needed (inferred).
The unsigned int* parameter, if provided, must point to writable memory; meaning is unknown. It may be NULL if not needed (inferred).
Returned pointer type/layout depends on stash_type and is unspecified; callers must cast appropriately and must not assume ownership or mutability unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: pr_stash_remove_symbol
functions.signature: int pr_stash_remove_symbol(pr_stash_type_t stash_type, const char *name, module *m);
functions.description: Removes a previously-registered symbol, identified by name, from the stash of the given type and associated with the specified module. Intended for modules to unregister their symbols. Return value semantics are not documented here; success/failure details are unknown.

functions.description: Removes a command handler symbol matching the provided criteria (command name plus optional type/group/class) for the given module. Specialized form of pr_stash_remove_symbol for PR_SYM_CMD. Return value semantics are unknown.

cmd must be one of: PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_ENT_INSERT, PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_ENT_REMOVE, PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_FLAGS, PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_KEY_CMP, PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_KEY_HASH, PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_NCHAINS, PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_MAX_ENTS

For PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_KEY_HASH: arg must be a pointer to a function with signature unsigned int (*)(const void *key, size_t keysz), or NULL to use default
For PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_NCHAINS: arg must encode the desired number of chains (default 256); exact arg type not specified in header
For PR_TABLE_CTL_SET_MAX_ENTS: arg must encode the desired maximum entries (default 8192); exact arg type not specified in header

A NUL-terminated string consisting of one or more delimiter characters used by tokenizers (e.g., strsep). Should not contain NUL within the set; any byte values are otherwise allowed.
A shell-style glob pattern string used by glob(3) (supports wildcards like *, ?, and character classes). It is a NUL-terminated path pattern.
A NUL-terminated string representing either a DNS hostname (e.g., example.com) or a numeric IP literal (IPv4 like 192.0.2.1 or IPv6 like 2001:db8::1).
A NUL-terminated string specifying a service for network APIs, either a well-known service name (e.g., "http", "ftp") or a decimal port number (e.g., "80").
A NUL-terminated string that should be a numeric IPv4 or IPv6 literal suitable for inet_pton (e.g., 203.0.113.5 or 2001:db8::5).

A byte sequence used to fill binary structures (e.g., sockaddr fields or raw address bytes). The bytes are not interpreted as text; length may be shorter than the target buffer, with remaining bytes zeroed.
A NUL-terminated string intended to represent a single argv token for getopt-style parsing. May begin with '-' to indicate an option or contain arbitrary text as a non-option argument.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to generate a single bytes buffer that the fuzz harness will slice
# to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(), and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# The stubs here use:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times (general C strings)
# - FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) multiple times
# There is no FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in the provided stubs.
#
# Strategy:
# Build a small binary container with a header indicating how many unsigned
# ints and how many strings follow, then serialize them. Strings are
# NUL-terminated and limited in length to safe bounds for the stubs.
# This yields valid C strings and plentiful integers.
#
# Container format (all little-endian):
# [magic 4 bytes: b"FZIN"]
# [u16 num_uints]
# [u16 num_strings]
# [num_uints * 4 bytes of uint32]
# Then strings: for each, [u16 len] [len bytes payload] [0x00 terminator]
# Total size limited to <= 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_STR_LEN = 256  # cap individual strings; stubs also cap further

SAFE_CHARS = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:/@#%+[](){}<>^$!~?*|=\t\n"
)


def _rand_uint(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Provide a mixture of edge and random values
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF]
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        return r.choice(choices) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return r.getrandbits(32)


def _rand_str(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct strings that are useful for snprintf/strsep/glob_pattern_p
    kinds = [
        "plain",
        "words",
        "csv",
        "path",
        "glob",
        "percent",
        "unicode",
    ]
    kind = r.choice(kinds)

    if kind == "plain":
        s = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 40)))
    elif kind == "words":
        words = ["alpha", "beta", "Gamma", "delta", "epsilon"]
        s = ' '.join(r.choice(words) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)))
    elif kind == "csv":
        tokens = [''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 6))) for __ in range(r.randint(1, 8))]
        s = ','.join(tokens)
    elif kind == "path":
        segs = ["/", "./", "../", "/var", "/tmp", "/home", "user", "data", "file.txt"]
        depth = r.randint(1, 5)
        s = ''.join(r.choice(segs) for _ in range(depth))
    elif kind == "glob":
        # Include metacharacters for glob_pattern_p
        parts = [
            r.choice(["*", "?", "[a-z]", "[!0-9]", "file", "name", "data", "log"])
            for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))
        ]
        s = ''.join(parts)
    elif kind == "percent":
        # Include percent signs for snprintf literal percent scenario
        s = "percent=% done " + ''.join(r.choice("0123456789") for _ in range(r.randint(0, 5)))
    else:  # unicode
        # Valid UTF-8 sequences mixed with ASCII
        pool = [
            "α", "β", "γ", "д", "Ж", "漢", "字", "€", "✓", "™",
            " ", "-", "_", ".", "/", "@"
        ]
        s = ''.join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 20)))

    # Occasionally craft delimiter sets for strsep
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        delims = r.choice([",;:", "|/", " \t", ".,", ":@"])
        s = s + r.choice(["", " "]) + delims

    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:MAX_STR_LEN]
    return b


def _pack_u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF))


def _pack_u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((
        n & 0xFF,
        (n >> 8) & 0xFF,
        (n >> 16) & 0xFF,
        (n >> 24) & 0xFF,
    ))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide counts with bias to small, non-zero values
    num_uints = r.randint(6, 20)
    num_strings = r.randint(6, 20)

    out = bytearray()
    out += b"FZIN"
    out += _pack_u16(num_uints)
    out += _pack_u16(num_strings)

    # Add integers
    for _ in range(num_uints):
        out += _pack_u32(_rand_uint(r))
        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL - 64:
            break

    # Add strings
    for _ in range(num_strings):
        s = _rand_str(r)
        # Ensure no interior NUL; already guaranteed by encoding, but replace if any
        s = s.replace(b"\x00", b"_")
        if len(out) + 2 + len(s) + 1 >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += _pack_u16(len(s))
        out += s
        out += b"\x00"

    # Ensure we end with at least one NUL for robustness
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        if len(out) < MAX_TOTAL:
            out += b"\x00"

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import string

# Target: generate interesting, valid printf format strings (NUL-terminated)
# The fuzzer stub picks among several fixed formats, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR() is used
# as a %s argument for sel==0, and snprintf always needs a valid C string.
# We'll provide a corpus of diverse, valid printf format strings which exercise
# flags, widths, precisions, length modifiers, percent escaping, pointers, etc.
# The buffer returned must be bytes; we will NUL-terminate it.

_FMT_SIMPLE = [
    b"%d %u %s",           # matches sel==0
    b"%p",                  # matches sel==1
    b"val=%lld",            # matches sel==2
    b"percent=%% done",     # matches sel==3
]

# Additional valid formats to broaden coverage for printf parser (even if not used
# by this stub directly, they are valid and may seed mutations in other harnesses).
_FMT_RICH = [
    b"%-10d %+08d % 6u %s",
    b"[%#x] [%#06o] %s",
    b"%.0f %.3f %e %g %s",
    b"%hhd %hhu %hd %hu %ld %lu %lld %llu",
    b"% .4f %-#12.6x %s",
    b"%*.*s",  # requires two ints then string; still valid seed text
    b"%zu %td %jd %s",
    b"%#llx %p %s",
    b"%.s %% %% %% %s",
    b"%-20.10s",
]

# Valid UTF-8 strings to supply for %s arguments in sel==0 branch. Keep ASCII-safe.
_STR_CORPUS = [
    "hello",
    "",
    "A" * 1,
    "B" * 127,
    "quick-brown-fox",
    "lines\\nwith\\nslashes",
    "tab\tseparated",
    "path:/var/log/proftpd",
    "email:user@example.com",
    "json:{\"k\":\"v\"}",
]


def _pick_weighted(rng, items):
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]


def _make_format(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # 60%: choose one of the formats the stub uses directly (guaranteed valid)
    # 40%: choose a richer valid printf format string
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        fmt = _pick_weighted(rng, _FMT_SIMPLE)
    else:
        fmt = _pick_weighted(rng, _FMT_RICH)
    return fmt


def _maybe_embed_string_arg(rng):
    # Build a plausible %s argument payload to accompany format-oriented fuzzers
    s = rng.choice(_STR_CORPUS)
    # Occasionally extend with random safe chars (ASCII letters/digits/punct)
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        extra_len = rng.randint(0, 48)
        extra = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:@, ") for _ in range(extra_len))
        s = s + extra
    # Cap length to 128 to match harness truncation
    if len(s) > 128:
        s = s[:128]
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    fmt = _make_format(seed ^ 0x9E3779B185EBCA87)

    # Build a payload that includes:
    # - the format string (NUL-terminated)
    # - optionally one or more string arguments separated by NULs, so that
    #   FUZZ_PARAM_STR() reads a reasonable %s string from the buffer.
    # Many fuzzers feed the same initial buffer into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_*; adding
    # an extra NUL-terminated %s argument after the format increases validity.

    parts = [fmt + b"\x00"]

    # Provide at least one %s argument string for sel==0; harmless for other cases.
    sarg = _maybe_embed_string_arg(rng) + b"\x00"
    parts.append(sarg)

    # Optionally add a second %s candidate
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_maybe_embed_string_arg(rng) + b"\x00")

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4095] + b"\x00"
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: generate buffers suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as:
# 1) a mutable buffer to tokenize (arbitrary text, up to 512 bytes)
# 2) a delimiter string (non-empty, NUL-terminated C string, <=16 chars, no embedded NUL)
# The fuzzer stub uses two FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls; typical harnesses will split
# the provided bytes into successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumptions. We therefore
# craft a single bytes blob that encodes two strings in sequence, each NUL-terminated.
#
# Format we emit:
#   [tokenizable_text]\x00[delimiter_set]\x00
#
# We aim to create interesting tokenizable_text with various patterns (empty tokens,
# consecutive delimiters, leading/trailing delimiters, quoted-like pieces, UTF-8, etc.)
# and delimiter sets that vary (commas, whitespace, punctuation, mixed chars).

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_DELIM_POOLS: List[str] = [
    ",",
    " ",
    "\t",
    ":",
    "|",
    ",;",
    " \t",
    "::",
    "|,",
    ",|;:\t ",
    "/",
    "-",
]

# Some reusable token components to create varied content
_WORDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon", "zeta", "eta", "theta",
    "iota", "kappa", "lambda", "mu", "nu", "xi", "omicron", "pi", "rho",
    "sigma", "tau", "upsilon", "phi", "chi", "psi", "omega",
]

def _rand_delims(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a delimiter set, 1..8 chars, unique, from a chosen pool or custom
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        base = r.choice(_DELIM_POOLS)
        # maybe augment base
        extras = ''.join(r.sample(",;|:\t -/_", r.randint(0, 3)))
        s = ''.join(dict.fromkeys((base + extras)))  # unique preserve order
    else:
        # Construct random delimiters from punctuation/space
        candidates = ",;|:\t -/_\n\r\f\v."
        k = r.randint(1, min(8, len(candidates)))
        s = ''.join(dict.fromkeys(r.sample(candidates, k)))
    # Ensure no NUL and non-empty
    if not s:
        s = ","
    return s.replace('\x00', ',')[:16]

def _make_text(r: random.Random, delims: str, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Compose text with patterns relative to the delimiters to exercise strsep
    parts: List[str] = []
    D = delims
    # Some common patterns
    patterns = []
    # Leading delimiters => empty first tokens
    patterns.append(D * r.randint(1, 4))
    # Words separated by single delimiter
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        word = r.choice(_WORDS)
        patterns.append(word)
        patterns.append(r.choice(D))
    # Multiple consecutive delimiters for empty tokens
    patterns.append(r.choice(D) * r.randint(2, 5))
    # Trailing delimiters => empty last tokens
    patterns.append(r.choice(D) * r.randint(1, 3))
    # Mixed tokens including numbers and unicode
    nums = [str(r.randint(0, 99999)) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5))]
    patterns.append(r.choice(D).join(nums))
    # Embed some quoted-like substrings containing delimiters (not special to strsep, but interesting)
    q = '"'
    patterns.append(q + r.choice(_WORDS) + r.choice(D) + r.choice(_WORDS) + q)
    # Add whitespace blocks if not already in delimiters, to vary token spans
    patterns.append(" ")
    # Combine and then sprinkle additional random delimiters
    s = ''.join(patterns)
    # Insert random delimiters at random positions
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 10)):
        pos = r.randint(0, len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + r.choice(D) * r.randint(1, 3) + s[pos:]
    # Ensure within target_len; optionally pad or trim
    if len(s) < target_len // 2:
        # pad with alternating word and delimiter
        while len(s) < target_len // 2:
            s += r.choice(D) + r.choice(_WORDS)
    if len(s) > target_len:
        s = s[:target_len]
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose delimiter set first so we can craft text accordingly
    delims = _rand_delims(r)

    # Decide sizes
    # Total must be <= 4096 including two NULs
    # strsep fuzzer limits first string to 512; we target up to that.
    text_max = 512
    text_len = r.randint(0, text_max)  # allow empty too
    text = _make_text(r, delims, text_len)

    # Occasionally force edge cases for tokenization
    mode = r.random()
    if mode < 0.2:
        # Only delimiters (many empties)
        text = delims * r.randint(1, max(1, min(50, text_max // max(1, len(delims)))))
    elif mode < 0.35:
        # No delimiters present -> single token
        # Replace delimiters in text with non-delimiter characters
        rep = '_'
        for d in delims:
            text = text.replace(d, rep)
    elif mode < 0.45:
        # Alternate empty and word
        text = ''.join((r.choice([d for d in delims]) + r.choice(_WORDS)) for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)))
        # End with delimiter to create trailing empty
        text += r.choice(delims)

    # Ensure delimiter string is non-empty and has no NUL; trim to <=16
    delim_str = delims[:16] or ","

    # Assemble as two C strings: text\0delim\0
    enc = text.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    delim_enc = delim_str.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

    out = bytearray()
    out += enc
    out += b"\x00"
    out += delim_enc
    out += b"\x00"

    # Enforce max size
    return bytes(out[:_MAX_TOTAL])

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generate a variety of valid filesystem glob patterns. These are NUL-terminated C strings
# when used by the target; here we just return bytes (without embedded NUL) suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Goals:
# - Exercise *, ?, [] character classes
# - Include brace-like ranges inside []
# - Include path separators to trigger multi-segment matching
# - Include leading dot names (., .., .hidden)
# - Mix escaped characters (although flags may disable escapes)
# - Include patterns that likely match something on many systems (/, /*, /tmp/*) and purely synthetics
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes

_PATH_SEPS = ["/"]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(0, len(seq))]

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=10, allow_dot_start=True) -> str:
    # Allowed chars typical for filenames
    alpha = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    extra = "-_.@#%+="
    chars = alpha + extra
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))
    if not allow_dot_start and s.startswith('.'):
        s = 'f' + s
    return s

def _char_class(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build something like [abc], [a-z], [!0-9], [[:alpha:]]
    types = [
        lambda: "[a-z]",
        lambda: "[A-Z]",
        lambda: "[0-9]",
        lambda: "[!0-9]",
        lambda: "[abcxyz]",
        lambda: "[[:alpha:]]",
        lambda: "[[:alnum:]]",
        lambda: "[[:digit:]]",
        lambda: "[![:space:]]",
    ]
    return _rand_choice(rng, [t() for t in types])

def _segment_with_wildcards(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a segment mixing literals and wildcards
    parts = []
    choices = [
        lambda: '*',
        lambda: '?',
        lambda: _char_class(rng),
        lambda: _rand_filename(rng, 1, 6, allow_dot_start=True),
    ]
    k = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(k):
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, [c() for c in choices]))
    return ''.join(parts)

def _maybe_escape(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally escape a special char with backslash
    specials = ['*', '?', '[', ']', '\\']
    if not s:
        return s
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch in specials and rng.random() < 0.2:
            out.append('\\' + ch)
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)

def _build_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    patterns = []

    # Some canonical, broadly matching roots
    roots = [
        '/',                # absolute root
        '/tmp',             # common temp
        '/var',             # common dir
        '.',                # current dir
        '..',               # parent dir
        '~',                # home-like (though glob may or may not expand)
        '',                 # relative
    ]

    root = _rand_choice(rng, roots)
    segs: List[str] = []

    # Decide number of segments (1..4)
    nsegs = rng.randint(1, 4)

    for i in range(nsegs):
        # Make first literal segments sometimes hidden
        if i == 0 and rng.random() < 0.2:
            seg = '.' + _segment_with_wildcards(rng)
        else:
            seg = _segment_with_wildcards(rng)
        seg = _maybe_escape(rng, seg)
        segs.append(seg)

    # Occasionally append a trailing slash request (GLOB_MARK may add one too)
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        trailing = ''
    else:
        trailing = ''

    # Join with path separators carefully
    if root in ('', '.', '..', '~'):
        pattern = '/'.join([root] + segs) if root else '/'.join(segs)
    else:
        pattern = root.rstrip('/') + '/' + '/'.join(segs)

    pattern += trailing

    # Keep length reasonable
    if len(pattern) > 200:
        pattern = pattern[:200]

    return pattern

def _prebaked_suite() -> List[str]:
    return [
        '*',
        '.*',
        '.*rc',
        '*.c',
        '*.h',
        '?.txt',
        '[a-z]*',
        '[!a-z]*',
        '[[:digit:]]*.log',
        '/**',                 # though ** is not standard everywhere, harmless as text
        '/tmp/*',
        '/var/*',
        './*',
        '../*',
        'src/*.[ch]',
        'build/*',
        'docs/[A-Z]*.md',
        '.*/*',
        '*/.git/*',
        '*/?[0-9]*',
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Mix a prebaked pattern (known-interesting) with a synthesized one
    candidates = _prebaked_suite()
    # Add several synthesized patterns
    for _ in range(10):
        candidates.append(_build_pattern(rng))

    # Randomly pick 1-3 patterns and occasionally concatenate using braces-like or alternation style
    count = rng.randint(1, 2)
    chosen = rng.sample(candidates, k=count)

    if count == 1:
        pattern = chosen[0]
    else:
        # Use alternation-like list: {a,b} (not POSIX glob, but some implementations with EXT/GNU flags accept)
        # Still valid as a plain string otherwise.
        pattern = '{' + ','.join(chosen) + '}'

    # Ensure not empty
    if not pattern:
        pattern = '*'

    # Bound total size
    b = pattern.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

import random
import struct
import ipaddress

# We generate buffers intended to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR() in stubs
# exercising pr_getaddrinfo(). The stub occasionally passes NULL for node
# and/or service based on other fuzzed ints, so we just provide interesting
# valid strings for both cases; the engine will sometimes ignore them.
#
# Strategy: produce a byte blob that decodes to two concatenated C-strings
# (node and service), separated by a NUL, plus an extra trailing NUL-safe
# padding. The fuzzer harness typically reads arbitrary strings from the
# buffer; providing multiple useful tokens increases chances that FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# pulls meaningful host/service values.
#
# We include:
# - Valid hostnames (simple, with subdomains, mixed case)
# - Valid IPv4 literals
# - Valid IPv6 literals (compressed, with scope id, with port-like service separate)
# - Common service names ("ftp", "http", "domain") and numeric ports ("21", "80", etc.)
# - Edge-but-valid names like single-label hosts and localhost
# - Internationalized-looking labels (ASCII only) to stay valid for getaddrinfo
#
# Total size kept <= 4096 bytes.

def _rand_ipv4(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Avoid multicast/invalid; pick unicast examples, including RFC5737 ranges
    choices = [
        (203, 0, 113),
        (198, 51, 100),
        (192, 0, 2),
        (8, 8, 8),
        (1, 1, 1),
    ]
    a, b, c = rnd.choice(choices)
    d = rnd.randint(1, 254)
    return f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"


def _rand_ipv6(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a valid IPv6, often using documentation prefix 2001:db8::/32
    hextets = [0] * 8
    hextets[0] = 0x2001
    hextets[1] = 0x0DB8
    for i in range(2, 8):
        hextets[i] = rnd.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
    # compress by finding a zero run; simple approach: rely on ipaddress
    addr = ":".join(f"{h:x}" for h in hextets)
    try:
        return ipaddress.IPv6Address(addr).compressed
    except Exception:
        return "2001:db8::1"


def _rand_hostname(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a valid hostname: labels 1-63 chars, total <= 253
    labels_pool = [
        "example", "test", "dev", "prod", "staging", "alpha", "beta",
        "edge", "node", "api", "cdn", "mail", "ftp", "srv", "db",
    ]
    # ensure first/last are alnum; interior may contain hyphens
    def mk_label():
        base = rnd.choice(labels_pool)
        # chance to add numeric suffix or hyphen piece
        parts = [base]
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(str(rnd.randint(1, 9999)))
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            parts.insert(1, "-")
        lab = "".join(parts)
        lab = lab.strip("-")[:63]
        if not lab:
            lab = "host"
        return lab

    nlabels = rnd.randint(2, 4)
    labels = [mk_label() for _ in range(nlabels - 1)] + [rnd.choice(["com", "net", "org", "local", "example"]) ]
    hostname = ".".join(labels)
    return hostname[:253]


def _rand_service(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    services = [
        "ftp", "http", "https", "domain", "ntp", "ssh", "smtp", "pop3",
        "imap", "ldap", "kerberos",
    ]
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return rnd.choice(services)
    # numeric port 1..65535
    return str(rnd.randint(1, 65535))


def _build_c_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure ASCII and NUL-terminated when concatenated; replace any internal NULs.
    s = s.replace("\x00", " ")
    try:
        b = s.encode("ascii", "ignore")
    except Exception:
        b = s.encode()
    return b + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide a node kind
    node_kind = rnd.choice(["hostname", "ipv4", "ipv6", "localhost", "singlelabel"])
    if node_kind == "hostname":
        node = _rand_hostname(rnd)
    elif node_kind == "ipv4":
        node = _rand_ipv4(rnd)
    elif node_kind == "ipv6":
        node = _rand_ipv6(rnd)
    elif node_kind == "localhost":
        node = rnd.choice(["localhost", "ip6-localhost", "loopback.local"])  # valid-ish
    else:
        # single-label host (often valid in local resolvers)
        node = rnd.choice(["router", "gateway", "printer", "nas"])  # simple

    service = _rand_service(rnd)

    # Also include alternates to increase chances any FUZZ_PARAM_STR() call
    # pulls a meaningful token from this same buffer.
    alternates = [
        _rand_hostname(rnd),
        _rand_ipv4(rnd),
        _rand_ipv6(rnd),
        "example.com",
        "2001:db8::1",
        "192.0.2.10",
        "ftp",
        "21",
        "http",
        "80",
    ]

    parts = []
    parts.append(_build_c_string(node))
    parts.append(_build_c_string(service))

    # Add a second node/service pair
    parts.append(_build_c_string(rnd.choice(alternates)))
    parts.append(_build_c_string(_rand_service(rnd)))

    # Append a few extra tokens
    for _ in range(4):
        parts.append(_build_c_string(rnd.choice(alternates)))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Trim to max 4096 bytes
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4095] + b"\x00"
    return blob

import random
import struct
import itertools

# We generate byte buffers intended to be used as fuzzer-provided strings for
# pr_getaddrinfo() node/service inputs. The stubs sometimes pass NULL instead
# of the strings, but when used, valid inputs should exercise different code
# paths: IPv4/IPv6 literals, hostnames (with/without dots), and service names
# or numeric ports. We concatenate multiple NUL-terminated strings so the
# fuzzing harness can slice from the buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
#
# We keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

WELL_KNOWN_SERVICES = [
    "http", "https", "ftp", "ftps", "ssh", "telnet", "smtp", "imap", "pop3",
    "dns", "ntp", "ldap", "rdp", "mysql", "postgres", "redis", "memcached",
]

NUMERIC_PORTS = ["0", "21", "22", "25", "53", "67", "68", "80", "110", "123", "143", "389", "443", "5432", "6379", "65535"]

HOSTNAMES = [
    "localhost",
    "example.com",
    "www.example.org",
    "xn--exmple-cua.tld",  # punycode-like (tests UTF-8 bytes)
    "intranet",
    "srv01.local",
]

IPV4S = [
    "0.0.0.0",
    "127.0.0.1",
    "8.8.8.8",
    "1.2.3.4",
    "255.255.255.255",
]

IPV6S = [
    "::",
    "::1",
    "2001:db8::1",
    "fe80::1",
    "2001:4860:4860::8888",
]

# Service-name-or-port strings (data type focus)
SERVICE_STRINGS = WELL_KNOWN_SERVICES + NUMERIC_PORTS

# Node candidates for getaddrinfo's node parameter
NODE_STRINGS = HOSTNAMES + IPV4S + IPV6S

# Some additional variants to increase coverage: bracketed IPv6, host:port-like
EXTRA_NODES = ["[::1]", "[2001:db8::1]", "example.net", "sub.domain.example"]

# Build a few combined strings that include edge cases: empty string is valid C string
EDGE_STRINGS = ["", "0", "65535", "80\u0000trail"]


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _make_null_terminated(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure UTF-8 encoding and NUL termination; strip any embedded NULs after first segment
    if isinstance(s, bytes):
        b = s
    else:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', 'strict')
    # Stop at first NUL to avoid embedded terminators confusing consumers
    nul_pos = b.find(b"\x00")
    if nul_pos != -1:
        b = b[:nul_pos]
    return b + b"\x00"


def _build_catalog(rng):
    catalog = []
    # Mix of nodes and services to cover both parameters in different combinations
    # Include a balanced set of IPv4, IPv6, hostnames, and services
    for s in itertools.islice(itertools.cycle(NODE_STRINGS + EXTRA_NODES), 0, 20):
        catalog.append(s)
    for s in itertools.islice(itertools.cycle(SERVICE_STRINGS), 0, 20):
        catalog.append(s)
    # Add some edge/simple values
    catalog.extend(EDGE_STRINGS)
    # Random numeric ports in range
    for _ in range(10):
        catalog.append(str(rng.randint(0, 65535)))
    # Random-looking hostnames (valid label characters)
    for _ in range(10):
        labels = ["srv", str(rng.randint(0, 9999)), _rand_choice(rng, ["dev", "prod", "stg", "test"])]
        domain = _rand_choice(rng, ["local", "example.com", "corp.local", "lan"]) \
                 if rng.random() < 0.5 else "example.org"
        hn = "-".join(labels) + "." + domain
        catalog.append(hn)
    return catalog


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a catalog and then pick a random subset/order for this seed
    catalog = _build_catalog(rng)
    rng.shuffle(catalog)

    # Decide how many strings to emit; ensure at least a few node/service options
    n = rng.randint(8, 32)
    chosen = catalog[:n]

    # Compose as a sequence of NUL-terminated C strings back-to-back.
    out = bytearray()

    # Optionally prefix with a small header of random bytes to vary FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) reads
    # (the stub uses FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for toggles and family/proto selection)
    prefix_count = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(prefix_count):
        out += struct.pack('<I', rng.getrandbits(32))

    for s in chosen:
        b = _make_null_terminated(s)
        # Keep total size within limit
        if len(out) + len(b) > 4096:
            break
        out += b

    # Ensure we have at least one service string and one node string present
    needed = []
    if not any(x in SERVICE_STRINGS or x.isdigit() for x in chosen):
        needed.append(_rand_choice(rng, SERVICE_STRINGS))
    if not any(x in NODE_STRINGS or x in EXTRA_NODES for x in chosen):
        needed.append(_rand_choice(rng, NODE_STRINGS + EXTRA_NODES))
    for s in needed:
        b = _make_null_terminated(s)
        if len(out) + len(b) <= 4096:
            out += b
        else:
            break

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: provide binary data used by fuzz stubs to populate sockaddr/in_addr/in6_addr fields.
# Interesting cases:
# - IPv4: 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 255.255.255.255, multicast 224.x, private ranges, broadcast patterns
# - IPv6: ::, ::1, IPv4-mapped ::ffff:*, link-local fe80::, multicast ff02::, 2001:db8:: doc, random
# - Ports: 0, 1, 21, 53, 80, 123, 443, 65535, random
# Fuzzer stub reads first 2 bytes as port (little-endian) then next 4 or 16 bytes as address.
# It may also use the same buffer for pr_inet_ntop which consumes 4/16 bytes.
# We therefore emit sequences sized to cover both cases (at least 18 bytes for IPv6 path),
# but we can vary sizes too; the stub pads missing bytes with zeros, which is fine.


DEF_PORTS = [0, 1, 7, 20, 21, 22, 23, 25, 53, 67, 68, 69, 80, 110, 123, 143, 161, 389, 443, 587, 993, 995, 2049, 3306, 5432, 6379, 8080, 8443, 49152, 65535]

DEF_IPv4 = [
    (0, 0, 0, 0),         # INADDR_ANY
    (127, 0, 0, 1),       # loopback
    (255, 255, 255, 255), # broadcast
    (192, 168, 1, 1),     # private
    (10, 0, 0, 1),        # private
    (172, 16, 0, 1),      # private
    (224, 0, 0, 1),       # multicast
    (8, 8, 8, 8),         # public DNS
    (1, 1, 1, 1),         # public DNS
]

DEF_IPv6 = [
    bytes(16),                                # ::
    (b"\x00"*15 + b"\x01"),                 # ::1
    bytes.fromhex('fe800000000000000000000000000001'),  # fe80::1 (link-local)
    bytes.fromhex('ff020000000000000000000000000001'),  # ff02::1 (multicast)
    bytes.fromhex('20010db8000000000000000000000001'),  # 2001:db8::1 (doc)
    # IPv4-mapped ::ffff:127.0.0.1
    bytes.fromhex('00000000000000000000ffff7f000001'),
]


def _pack_le_word16(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', v & 0xFFFF)


def _choose_ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(0, len(DEF_IPv4) + 3)
    if choice < len(DEF_IPv4):
        a, b, c, d = DEF_IPv4[choice]
    elif choice == len(DEF_IPv4):
        # sequential increasing
        base = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        a, b, c, d = base, (base + 1) % 256, (base + 2) % 256, (base + 3) % 256
    elif choice == len(DEF_IPv4) + 1:
        # random
        a, b, c, d = [rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(4)]
    else:
        # net/broadcast boundary
        net = rng.choice([(10, 0, 0), (192, 168, 0), (172, 16, 0)])
        a, b, c = net
        d = rng.choice([0, 1, 255])
    return bytes([a, b, c, d])


def _choose_ipv6(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(0, len(DEF_IPv6) + 3)
    if choice < len(DEF_IPv6):
        return DEF_IPv6[choice]
    elif choice == len(DEF_IPv6):
        # random 128-bit
        return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
    elif choice == len(DEF_IPv6) + 1:
        # IPv4-mapped with random v4
        v4 = _choose_ipv4(rng)
        return bytes.fromhex('00000000000000000000ffff') + v4
    else:
        # embed a pattern: alternating bytes
        return bytes((i * 17) & 0xFF for i in range(16))


def _build_ipv4_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    port = rng.choice(DEF_PORTS)
    ip = _choose_ipv4(rng)
    return _pack_le_word16(port) + ip


def _build_ipv6_packet(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    port = rng.choice(DEF_PORTS)
    ip6 = _choose_ipv6(rng)
    return _pack_le_word16(port) + ip6


def _maybe_truncate_or_pad(buf: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # The stub pads to 6 (IPv4) or 18 (IPv6) if shorter; keep variety
    modes = ['full', 'short', 'padextra']
    m = rng.choice(modes)
    if m == 'full':
        return buf
    if m == 'short':
        # truncate to a random shorter length but at least 1
        new_len = rng.randrange(1, max(2, len(buf)))
        return buf[:new_len]
    # pad with zeros to a random larger size up to 32
    pad_to = rng.randrange(len(buf), min(32, len(buf) + 8) + 1)
    return buf.ljust(pad_to, b"\x00")


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide to produce IPv4-style or IPv6-style oriented buffer
    ipv6_bias = rng.random()
    if ipv6_bias < 0.5:
        pkt = _build_ipv4_packet(rng)
    else:
        pkt = _build_ipv6_packet(rng)

    pkt = _maybe_truncate_or_pad(pkt, rng)

    # Sometimes concatenate an extra unrelated chunk to vary pr_inet_ntop path
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        extra = rng.choice([
            _choose_ipv4(rng),
            _choose_ipv6(rng)[:4],
            os.urandom(rng.randrange(1, 5))
        ])
        pkt += extra

    # Ensure overall size reasonable
    return pkt[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate bytes for a corpus input that will be split by the fuzzer into
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() uses. The target stub constructs argv with up to
# 5 entries (prog + up to 4 FUZZ_PARAM_STR). The getopt optstring is "ab:c::d"
# meaning:
#  -a and -d: no argument
#  -b ARG: requires argument (next argv token or attached)
#  -c[=ARG]: optional argument (GNU extension), can be attached or separate
# We thus craft a sequence of tokens that exercise:
#  - pure flags (-a, -d)
#  - required-arg in attached form (-bVALUE) and separate form (-b VALUE)
#  - optional-arg for -c in three forms: no arg (-c), attached (-cVALUE), separate (-c VALUE)
#  - a mix of non-option operands ("--", filenames, plain words)
# The fuzzer will pull strings sequentially; we embed them NUL-separated so the
# harness can slice them. The function returns bytes containing NUL-terminated
# tokens.

MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 4096


def _rand_word(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=10) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_+."
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _build_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens: List[str] = []

    # Always start with a plausible option to ensure getopt progresses.
    tokens.append("-a")  # simple flag

    # Add -b with required argument in either attached or separate form.
    b_arg = _rand_word(rng, 1, 12)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tokens.append("-b" + b_arg)  # attached
    else:
        tokens.extend(["-b", b_arg])  # separate

    # Add -c with optional argument: randomly choose form.
    form = rng.randrange(3)
    if form == 0:
        tokens.append("-c")  # no arg
    elif form == 1:
        tokens.append("-c" + _rand_word(rng, 0, 10))  # attached (possibly empty)
    else:
        tokens.extend(["-c", _rand_word(rng, 0, 10)])  # separate

    # Possibly add -d flag
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        tokens.append("-d")

    # Add a mix of non-option arguments and the option-terminator "--"
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tokens.append("--")
    # After --, add 0-2 positional operands
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        tokens.append(_rand_word(rng, 1, 15))

    # Add some edge-case tokens to stress parsing but remain valid C strings
    edge_pool = [
        "-",               # lone dash
        "-a-",             # looks like option then non-option
        "-b=val",          # not standard attached style but valid token
        "-c=",             # optional arg with equals
        "-dd",             # combined flags-like token
        _rand_word(rng, 20, 32),  # long operand
        "",                # empty -> harness will replace with "-a", but include for variety
    ]
    rng.shuffle(edge_pool)
    # Add 0-3 of these
    tokens.extend(edge_pool[:rng.randint(0, 3)])

    # Ensure we have between 1 and 4 tokens available for FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    # The stub may request up to 4 strings. We'll provide at least 4 by padding.
    while len(tokens) < 4:
        # Alternate between a flag and an operand
        tokens.append(rng.choice(["-a", "-d", _rand_word(rng, 1, 12)]))

    # Trim excessive tokens to keep total size reasonable when NUL-joined
    return tokens[:8]


def _to_bytes(tokens: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join tokens as NUL-terminated segments, suitable for splitting.
    # Ensure each token is encoded in UTF-8; append a final NUL.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for t in tokens:
        parts.append(t.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL_BYTES]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    tokens = _build_tokens(rng)
    return _to_bytes(tokens)
